1. 音频效果和自动化

1. Audio Effects And Automation









1.1. 压缩机

1.1. Compressors

小即是大——塞思·戈丁

Small is the new big - Seth Godin









你听到的几乎所有音乐和录音都至少在制作过程中经过了一次压缩。如果你认真对待音乐制作，就必须熟悉这个强大的工具。这意味着不仅要了解其整体原理，还要深入了解每个参数（阈值、压缩比、启动时间、释放时间、增益补偿）。

Almost all music and recorded speech that you hear has been sent through at least one compressor at some point during the production process. If you are serious about music production, you need to get familiar with this powerful tool. This means understanding the big picture as well as getting to know each of the parameters (Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release, Make-Up Gain) intimately.









  • 它们是如何运作的

  • How They Work





在任何一首歌中，音量都会随时间变化。例如，主歌部分音量可能在 -6 分贝左右，第一段副歌部分上升到 -2 分贝，间奏部分下降到 -8 分贝，以此类推。在这个语境下，一个值得了解的术语是动态范围。它指的是从最轻柔到最响亮的音量差异。某些音乐类型，例如管弦乐，通常具有较大的动态范围，而主流流行乐和摇滚乐则更倾向于较小的动态范围。一首交响乐的动态范围可能从柔和的双簧管独奏的 -20 分贝到激动人心的结尾和弦的 -2 分贝（动态范围：18 分贝），而一首常见的流行歌曲的动态范围则通常是从第一段主歌的 -8 分贝到最后一段副歌的 0 分贝（动态范围：8 分贝）。

Throughout any song the volume level varies over time. It might hover around - 6 dB in the verse, rise to - 2 dB in the first chorus, drop to - 8 dB in the interlude, and so on. A term that is worth knowing in this context is the dynamic range. It refers to the difference in volume level from the softest to the loudest part. Some genres of music, such as orchestral music, generally have a large dynamic range, while for mainstream pop and rock a much smaller dynamic range is desired. A symphony might range from - 20 dB in the soft oboe solo to - 2 dB for the exciting final chord (dynamic range: 18 dB), whereas your common pop song will rather go from - 8 dB in the first verse to 0 dB in the last chorus (dynamic range: 8 dB).





录音过程中，我们可以对最终的动态范围进行一定程度的控制。我们可以告诉乐手在主歌部分轻柔一些，在副歌部分尽情发挥。当然，这种方法并不十分精确，我们希望能够完全控制动态范围，而不仅仅是部分控制。我们也希望能够在后期调整动态范围。压缩器能够实现这一切（以及更多功能）。

During a recording we have some control over what dynamic range we will end up with. We can tell the musicians to take it easy in the verse and really go for it in the chorus. But of course this is not very accurate and we'd like to have full control of the dynamic range rather than just some. We'd also like to be able to to change the dynamic range later on. Compressors make this (and much more) possible.





压缩机持续监测音量。只要音量低于某个阈值，压缩机就不会工作。只有当音量超过阈值时，它才会启动，并按一定比例衰减多余的音量。简而言之：低于阈值的音量保持不变，高于阈值的音量会被压缩。请记住这一点。

The compressor constantly monitors the volume level. As long as the level is below a certain threshold, the compressor will not do anything. Only when the level exceeds the threshold does it become active and dampen the excess volume by a certain ratio. In short: everything below the threshold stays as it is, everything above the threshold gets compressed. Keep this in mind.





例如，假设我们将阈值设置为 -10 dB，压缩比设置为 4:1。在应用压缩器之前，歌曲的音量从主歌部分的最小值 -12 dB 到副歌部分的最大值 -2 dB 不等。我们先来看主歌部分。此时音量没有超过阈值，因此压缩器不会启动。信号将保持不变地通过。副歌部分的情况则不同。它的音量比阈值高出 8 dB。压缩器会根据我们设定的压缩比对这部分多余的音量进行衰减。更具体地说：压缩器会将这 8 dB 的多余音量衰减到 8 dB / 4 = 2 dB。因此，压缩后的歌曲音量范围从主歌部分的 -12 dB 到副歌部分的 -10 dB + 2 dB = -8 dB。

Suppose for example we set the threshold to - 10 dB and the ratio to 4:1. Before applying the compressor, our song varies from a minimum value of - 12 dB in the verse to a maximum value - 2 dB in the chorus. Let's look at the verse first. Here the volume does not exceed the threshold and thus the compressor does not spring into action. The signal will pass through unchanged. The story is different for the chorus. Its volume level is 8 dB above the threshold. The compressor takes this excess volume and dampens it according to the ratio we set. To be more specific: the compressor turns the 8 dB excess volume into a mere 8 dB / 4 = 2 dB. So the compressed song ranges from - 12 dB in the verse to -10 dB + 2 dB = - 8 dB in the chorus.





以下是流程概述：

Here's a summary of the process:





设置：

Settings:





阈值：-10 dB

Threshold: - 10 dB

比例：4:1

Ratio: 4:1





前：

Before:





  • 最低值：-12 分贝

  • Minimum: - 12 dB

  • 最大值：-2 分贝

  • Maximum: - 2 dB

  • 动态范围：10 dB

  • Dynamic range: 10 dB





超额音量（阈值到最大值）：8 分贝

Excess volume (threshold to maximum): 8 dB

应用比率后：8 dB / 4 = 2 dB

With ratio applied: 8 dB / 4 = 2 dB





后：

After:

  • Minimum: - 12 dB

  • 最大值：-8 分贝

  • Maximum: - 8 dB

  • 动态范围：4 dB

  • Dynamic range: 4 dB





正如您所见，压缩器对动态范围产生了显著影响。通过选择合适的阈值和压缩比，我们可以自由地将歌曲压缩到所需的任何动态范围。使用 DAW（数字音频工作站，例如 Cubase、FL Studio 或 Ableton Live）时，您可以直观地看到压缩器的工作原理。下图显示了未压缩的文件（上）和压缩后的文件（下），其中阈值设置为 -12 dB，压缩比设置为 2:1。

As you can see, the compressor had a significant effect on the dynamic range. Choosing appropriate values for the threshold and ratio, we are free to compress the song to any dynamic range we desire. When using a DAW (Digital Audio Workstation such as Cubase, FL Studio or Ableton Live), it is possible to see the workings of a compressor with your own eyes. The image below shows the uncompressed file (top) and the compressed file (bottom) with the threshold set to - 12 dB and the ratio to 2:1.













轻柔的部分保持不变，而响亮的部分（包括短暂且可能存在问题的峰值）的音量则有所降低。动态范围在此过程中明显缩小。请注意，应用压缩器后，歌曲的有效音量（RMS）会显著降低。由于这通常不是我们想要的结果，大多数压缩器都提供了一个名为“补偿增益”的参数。您可以通过此参数指定压缩完成后，压缩器将歌曲音量提升多少。此音量提升应用于歌曲的所有部分，无论轻柔还是响亮，因此动态范围不会发生任何变化。它仅用于补偿响度损失（因此得名）。

The soft parts are identical, while the louder parts (including the short and possibly problematic peaks) have been reduced in volume. The dynamic range clearly shrunk in the process. Note that after applying the compressor, the song's effective volume (RMS) is much lower. Since this is usually not desired, most compressors have a parameter called make-up gain. Here you can specify by how much you'd like the compressor to raise the volume of the song after the compression process is finished. This increase in volume is applied to all parts of the song, soft or loud, so there will not be another change in the dynamic range. It only makes up for the loss in loudness (hence the name).









  • 压缩机的使用

  • Usage of Compressors





我们已经了解了压缩器的一个应用：控制歌曲的动态范围。但这通常只是实现另一个目标的第一步：提高歌曲的有效音量。假设你有一首动态范围为 10 dB 的歌曲，你想让它尽可能响亮。于是你把音量推子推到最大电平为 0 dB。根据动态范围，最小电平现在应该是 -10 dB。有效音量显然会在这两个值之间。为了简单起见，我们假设它正好在中间，即 -5 dB。但这对你来说太小了。该怎么办呢？

We already got to know one application of the compressor: controlling the dynamic range of a song. But usually this is just a first step in reaching another goal: increasing the effective volume of the song. Suppose you have a song with a dynamic range of 10 dB and you want to make it as loud as possible. So you move the volume fader until the maximum level is at 0 dB. According to the dynamic range, the minimum level will now be at - 10 dB. The effective volume will obviously be somewhere in-between the two values. For the sake of simplicity, we'll assume it to be right in the middle, at - 5 dB. But this is too soft for your taste. What to do?





你插入一个阈值为 -6 dB、压缩比为 3:1 的压缩器。从最小电平 -10 dB 到阈值 -6 dB 的 4 dB 范围保持不变，而从阈值 -6 dB 到最大电平 0 dB 的 6 dB 范围被压缩至 6 dB / 3 = 2 dB。因此，整体动态范围缩小至 4 dB + 2 dB = 6 dB。你再次调节音量推子，直到最大音量与 0 dB 重合。然而，这次最小音量会更高，达到 -6 dB，有效音量为 -3 dB（比我们最初的 -5 dB 有所提升）。任务完成，压缩和增益的组合确实提高了平均音量。

You insert a compressor with a threshold of - 6 dB and a ratio of 3:1. The 4 dB range from the minimum level - 10 dB to the threshold - 6 dB is unchanged, while the 6 dB range from the threshold - 6 dB to the maximum level 0 dB is compressed to 6 dB / 3 = 2 dB. So overall the dynamic range is reduced to 4 dB + 2 dB = 6 dB. Again you move the volume fader until the maximum volume level coincides with 0 dB. However, this time the minimum volume will be higher, at - 6 dB, and the effective volume at - 3 dB (up from the - 5 dB we started with). Mission accomplished, the combination of compression and gain indeed left us with a higher average volume.





理论上，这意味着我们可以通过压缩歌曲，然后再提高音量，将有效音量提升到几乎任何我们想要的值。我们甚至可以将整首歌的音量控制在接近 0 分贝。这种可能性导致了音乐制作领域的“响度战争”。为什么不顺应潮流呢？首先，你总是希望尽可能突出副歌部分。如果前奏和主歌已经以最大音量播放，就很难做到这一点。另一个原因是，大幅降低动态范围会扼杀歌曲中的表现力。那些高度依赖表现力的音乐（例如管弦乐和原声音乐）通常拥有最高的动态范围，这并非巧合。它们需要宽广的动态范围才能从表达宁静祥和过渡到表达毁灭性的绝望。请大声朗读并记住以下内容：音乐的表现力越强，你就越不应该压缩它。虽然一首电子舞曲或许可以在最大音量下播放，但一首抒情歌曲肯定不行。

In theory, this means we can get the effective volume up to almost any value we desire by compressing a song and then making it louder. We could have the whole song close to 0 dB. This possibility has led to a "loudness war" in music production. Why not go along with that? For one, you always want to put as much emphasis as possible on the hook. This is hard to do if the intro and verse is already blaring at maximum volume. Another reason is that severely reducing the dynamic range kills the expressive elements in your song. It is not a coincidence that music which strongly relies on expressive elements (orchestral and acoustic music) usually has the highest dynamic range. It needs the wide range to go from expressing peaceful serenity to expressing destructive desperation. Read the following out loud and memorize it: the more expression it has, the less you should compress. While a techno song might work at maximum volume, a ballad sure won't.

-------------------------------------





背景信息 - 声压级和响度

Background Info - SPL and Loudness





谈论声音的大小可能比想象中要复杂得多。问题在于，我们的大脑处理声音输入的方式并非线性。声压级翻倍的声波，在我们听来并不一定响亮两倍。因此，在表达声音的大小时，我们可以选择使用定义明确的物理量，例如声压级（但遗憾的是，声压级并不能反映人对声音大小的感知），或者使用主观的心理声学量，例如响度（响度难以准确定义和测量）。

Talking about how loud something is can be surprisingly complicated. The problem is that our brain does not process sound inputs in a linear fashion. A sound wave with twice the sound pressure does not necessarily seem twice as loud to us. So when expressing how loud something is, we can either do this by using well-defined physical quantities such as the sound pressure level (which unfortunately does not reflect how loud a person perceives something to be) or by using subjective psycho-acoustic quantities such as loudness (which is hard to define and measure properly).





声波是压力和密度的波动，它在介质中以取决于介质材料和温度的速度传播。对于20℃的空气，这个速度约为340米/秒。声压表示声波压力与周围空气压力的偏差。声压级（简称SPL）与有效声压的对数成正比。简而言之：声压越强，声压级越高。声压级用于客观地测量声音的响度。另一个重要的客观测量量是音量。音量衡量的是音频信号中包含的能量，因此与声压级密切相关。

Sound waves are pressure and density fluctuations that propagate at a material- and temperature-dependent speed in a medium. For air at 20 °C this speed is roughly 340 m/s. The quantity sound pressure expresses the deviation of the sound wave pressure from the pressure of the surrounding air. The sound pressure level, in short: SPL, is proportional to the logarithm of the effective sound pressure. Long story short: the stronger the sound pressure, the higher the SPL. The SPL is used to objectively measure how loud something is. Another important objective quantity for this purpose is the volume. It is a measure of how much energy is contained in an audio signal and thus closely related to the SPL.





响度是一个主观量，它反映了我们对声音大小的感知。由于我们的大脑具有高度非线性，音频信号的响度并非与其声压级（SPL）或音量大小成正比。相反，响度以一种复杂的方式取决于声压级、频率、声音持续时间、带宽等等。下图展示了响度、声压级和频率之间关系的近似示意图。

A subjective quantity that reflects how loud we perceive something to be is loudness. Due to our highly non-linear brains, the loudness of an audio signal is not simply proportional to its SPL or volume level. Rather, loudness depends in a complex way on the SPL, frequency, duration of the sound, its bandwidth, etc ... In the image below you can see an approximation of the relationship between loudness, SPL and frequency.













任何一条红色曲线都代表等响曲线。以下是解读图表的方法。请看最底部的红色曲线。它从 20 Hz 频率、75 dB SPL 的声压级开始，到 100 Hz 频率、25 dB SPL 的声压级结束。由于红色曲线代表等响曲线，我们可以得出结论：我们感知到的 20 Hz、75 dB SPL 的声音与 100 Hz、25 dB SPL 的声音一样响，即使从纯粹的物理角度来看，前者比后者响三倍（75 dB / 25 dB = 3）。

Any red curve is a curve of equal loudness. Here's how we can read the chart. Take a look at the red curve at the very bottom. It starts at 75 dB SPL and a frequency of 20 Hz and reaches 25 dB SPL at 100 Hz. Since the red curve is a curve of equal loudness, we can conclude we perceive a 75 dB SPL sound at 20 Hz to be just as loud as a 25 dB SPL sound at 100 Hz, even though from a purely physical point of view the first sound is three times as loud as the second (75 dB / 25 dB = 3).

（Cubase 中的压缩器）

(Compressor in Cubase)









  • 阈值和比率

  • Threshold and Ratio





理想的阈值是多少？这取决于你想要达到的效果。假设你将阈值设置得相对较高（例如，在混音效果良好的情况下设置为 -10 dB）。在这种情况下，压缩器在歌曲的大部分时间里都不会起作用，只会在副歌部分和短暂的峰值处介入。将阈值设置得较高，就相当于“削去高频”。如果你对整体动态范围感到满意，但希望混音效果不那么激进，那么这是一个合适的选择。

What's the ideal threshold to use? This depends on what you are trying to accomplish. Suppose you set the threshold at a relatively high value (for example - 10 dB in a good mix). In this case the compressor will be inactive for most of the song and only kick in during the hook and short peaks. With the threshold set to a high value, you are thus "taking the top off". This would be a suitable choice if you are happy with the dynamics in general, but would like to make the mix less aggressive.





如果使用较低的阈值（例如在混音效果好的情况下使用 -25 dB），效果会如何呢？在这种情况下，压缩器会在歌曲的大部分时间里保持激活状态，使整首歌听起来更加饱满。如果您想要大幅提升歌曲的响度，这一点值得考虑。一旦混音足够饱满，您就可以追求更高的有效音量。但是，低阈值压缩也可以为抒情歌曲增添温暖感，因此它并非只能用于追求响度的混音。

What about low thresholds (such as -25 dB in a good mix)? In this case the compressor will be active for the most part of the song and will make the entire song quite dense. This is something to consider if you aim to really push the loudness of the song. Once the mix is dense, you can go for a high effective volume. But a low threshold compression can also add warmth to a ballad, so it's not necessarily a tool restricted to usage in the loudness war.





接下来谈谈压缩比。如果将压缩比设置为较高的值（例如 5:1 或更高），就相当于告诉混音：压缩到阈值即可，不能再往上。超过阈值的部分会被大幅压缩，这对于处理那些过于刺耳、导致混音过于激进的峰值非常有效。这可能是由于军鼓音量过大或歌手经验不足造成的。无论原因是什么，精心选择的阈值和较高的压缩比都能有效地解决这个问题。但请注意，在这种情况下，压缩器应该应用于导致问题的音轨，而不是整个混音。

Onto the ratio. If you set the ratio to a high value (such as 5:1 and higher), you are basically telling the mix: to the threshold and no further. Anything past the threshold will be heavily compressed, which is great if you have pushy peaks that make a mix overly aggressive. This could be the result of a snare that's way too loud or an inexperienced singer. Whatever the cause, a carefully chosen threshold and a high ratio should take care of it in a satisfying manner. Note though that in this case the compressor should be applied to the track that is causing the problem and not the entire mix.





较低的压缩比（例如 2:1 或更小）会产生较为细微的效果。如果您想对已经听起来不错、只需稍加润色的混音应用压缩器，这样的数值就非常理想。混音会变得更加饱满，但其原有的特色仍能得以保留。

A low value for the ratio (such as 2:1 or smaller) will have a rather subtle effect. Such values are perfect if you want to apply the compressor to a mix that already sounds well and just needs a finishing touch. The mix will become a little more dense, but its character will be kept intact.









  • 攻击与释放

  • Attack and Release





我们之前忽略了两个重要的参数：启动时间和释放时间。启动时间参数可以让你指定音量超过阈值后压缩器介入的速度。启动时间较长（20毫秒或更长）的压缩器会让一些短暂的峰值通过。只要这些峰值不是过大，这未必是坏事。短暂的峰值（也称为瞬态）对于歌曲的活力和自然音色至关重要。较长的启动时间可以确保这些特性得以保留，并使压缩器的工作更加不明显。

There are two important parameters we have ignored so far: the attack and release. The attack parameter allows you to specify how quickly the compressor sets in once the volume level goes past the threshold. A compressor with a long attack (20 milliseconds or more) will let short peaks pass. As long as these peaks are not over-the-top, this is not necessarily a bad thing. The presence of short peaks, also called transients, is important for a song's liveliness and natural sound. A long attack makes sure that these qualities are preserved and that the workings of the compressor are less noticeable.





较短的启动时间（5毫秒或更短）可以产生清脆悦耳的声音，非常适合充满活力的音乐。但需要注意的是，如果启动时间过短，压缩器会抹杀瞬态，导致整个混音听起来平淡乏味。更糟糕的是，过短的启动时间还会导致咔嗒声和令人不安的“抽吸效应”。因此，在缩短启动时间时，务必注意这些问题。

A short attack (5 milliseconds or less) can produce a beautifully crisp sound that is suitable for energetic music. But it is important to note that if the attack is too short, the compressor will kill the transients and the whole mix will sound flat and bland. Even worse, a short attack can lead to clicks and a nervous "pumping effect". Be sure to watch out for those as you shorten the attack.





释放时间是指音量降至阈值以下后，压缩器停止工作的时间。它通常比启动时间长得多，但总体原理类似。较长的释放时间（600 毫秒或更长）可确保压缩效果更加柔和，而较短的释放时间（150 毫秒或更短）则可能产生类似抽吸的声音。

The release is the time for the compressor to become inactive once the volume level goes below the threshold. It is usually much longer than the attack, but the overall principles are similar. A long release (600 milliseconds or more) will make sure that the compression happens in a more subtle fashion, while a short release (150 milliseconds or less) can produce a pumping sound.





选择合适的释放时间以匹配歌曲的节奏总是明智之举（混响和延迟的时间参数也同样如此）。一种方法是根据歌曲的节拍（以每分钟节拍数 BPM 为单位）计算出每拍时间 TPB（以毫秒为单位），并以此值作为参考。



It is always a good idea to choose the release so that it fits the rhythm of your song (the same of course is true for temporal parameters in reverb and delay). One way to do this is to calculate the time per beat TPB in milliseconds from your song's tempo as measured in beats per minute BPM and use this value as the point of reference.



TPB [毫秒] = 60000 / BPM

TPB [ms] = 60000 / BPM





例如，在一首 BPM = 120 的歌曲中，一个节拍的持续时间为 TPB = 60000 / 120 = 500 毫秒。如果需要更长的释放时间，请使用其倍数（1000 毫秒、1500 毫秒等等）；如果需要更短的释放时间，请将其除以任意自然数（500 毫秒 / 2 = 250 毫秒，500 毫秒 / 3 = 167 毫秒，等等）。这样，压缩器就能与音乐的节奏同步“呼吸”。

For example, in a song with the tempo BPM = 120 the duration of one beat is TPB = 60000 / 120 = 500 ms. If you need a longer release, use a multiple of it (1000 ms, 1500 ms, and so on), for a shorter release divide it by any natural number (500 ms / 2 = 250 ms, 500 ms / 3 = 167 ms, and so on). This way the compressor will "breathe" in unison with your music.





如果您不确定如何设置起音和释放时间，可以先使用 20/200 法则：将起音时间设置为 20 毫秒，释放时间设置为 200 毫秒，然后逐步调整到理想值。或者，您也可以直接查看压缩器的预设参数，找到合适的设置。

If you are not sure where to start regarding attack and release, just make use of the 20/200-rule: Set the attack to 20 ms, the release to 200 ms and work towards the ideal values from there. Alternatively, you can always go through the presets of the compressor to find suitable settings.









  • 并行压缩

  • Parallel Compression





并行压缩是一种高级压缩技术，可以让你“两全其美”。它既能产生压缩器特有的厚重音色，又不会损失太多音轨的动态和瞬态信息。首先，复制音轨。保持原音轨不变，在复制的音轨上添加一个压缩器。将压缩器的压缩比设置为适中的值（例如 2.5:1），选择几毫秒的短启动时间和大约 300 毫秒的释放时间。同时播放两个音轨，并根据个人喜好调整音量推子。

Parallel compression is an advanced compression technique that will give you the "best of both worlds". It allows you to produce the dense sound so characteristic for compressors without giving up too much of the track's dynamics and transients. Start by duplicating the track. Leave the original track as it is and place a compressor on the duplicate track. Set the the compressor's ratio to a moderate value (for example 2.5:1), choose a short attack of several milliseconds and a release of around 300 milliseconds. Play both tracks and set the volume faders to your liking.





这种方法比直接压缩音轨好在哪里呢？我们已经提到，压缩器会限制音轨的动态范围，并抹杀一些瞬态信号（如果压缩时间过短，甚至会抹杀所有瞬态信号）。通过保留其中一条音轨的原始状态，我们可以确保歌曲的动态和活力不会丢失。

How is this better than simply compressing the track? We already noted that a compressor will limit the dynamic range of a track and kill some (if the attack is too short even all) transients. By keeping one of the tracks in its original form, we make sure that there's no danger of losing the dynamics and the liveliness of the song.





你可以把并行压缩理解为以特定百分比应用压缩器。例如，如果我们压缩其中一个音轨后，两个音轨的音量仍然相等，那么我们实际上就应用了 50% 的压缩率。通过移动音量推子，你可以自由选择压缩的程度。如果你觉得音轨失去了太多自然的声音，只需提高未压缩音轨的音量推子即可。如果你想要更饱满的声音，则反之亦然。这样，你就拥有了一个额外的（不可见的）压缩参数来优化你的声音。

You can think of parallel compression as a way of applying the compressor at a certain percentage. For example, if both tracks have an equal volume level after we compressed one of it, we basically applied the compressor at 50 %. By moving the volume faders you are free to choose to what degree the compression should take place. If you feel that the track is missing too much of its natural sound, you can simply move the volume fader of the unaltered track up. If you want a denser sound, you do the opposite. So you are left with an additional (invisible) compression parameter to optimize your sound.









  • 多频段压缩器

  • Multi-Band Compressors





到目前为止，我提到“压缩器”这个词时，实际上指的是单频段压缩器。但许多数字音频工作站（DAW）也提供了功能更强大的压缩工具：多频段压缩器。它乍一看可能有点吓人，但仔细研究后你会发现，它的大部分参数你其实都已经很熟悉了。所以不用担心。

Up to now, whenever I used the word compressor I actually referred to the single-band compressor. But many DAWs also give you the option of using an even more powerful compression tool: the multi-band compressor. It looks quite intimidating at first, but taking a closer look you will come to realize that you know most of its parameters already. So no need to panic.













（Cubase中的多频段压缩器）

(Multi-Band Compressor in Cubase)





多频段压缩器由多个单频段压缩器（通常为四个）组成，每个压缩器都限定在特定的带宽范围内。例如，第一个压缩器只分析和处理音乐中 16 到 150 Hz 之间的频段。第二个压缩器则覆盖 150 Hz 到 1000 Hz 的所有频率。以此类推。因此，每个单频段压缩器都有其专属的频段，并使用您已经熟悉的参数进行控制：阈值、压缩比、启动时间和释放时间。

The multi-band compressor consists of a number of single-band compressors (usually four) that are all limited to a certain bandwidth. For example, compressor number one only analyzes and alters the portion of your music that is between 16 and 150 Hz. Compressor number two covers all frequencies from 150 Hz to 1000 Hz. And so on. So each single-band compressor is given its own territory and rules it with the parameters you are already familiar with: threshold, ratio, attack and release.





大多数多频段压缩器都允许您自由选择频率范围，因此以下频段仅供参考。为了熟悉各个频段，请务必使用压缩器的独奏功能（在上图中，该功能位于右侧输入输出图的正下方）。即使您最终没有使用多频段压缩器，独奏各个频段也非常有帮助。

In most multi-band compressors you are free to choose the frequency ranges, so the following bands are just for guidance. To get familiar with the bands, make sure to use the compressor's solo function (which in the above picture is just below the input-output diagram on the right side). Soloing the bands is very instructive even if you don't end up using the multi-band compressor.





通常，最低频段（低音）的频率范围为 16 Hz 至 150 Hz，包含超低音、低沉的隆隆声、底鼓以及贝斯乐器的基音。这个频段是任何歌曲的基础，但过度使用会导致音乐很快变得浑浊不堪。下一个频段通常涵盖 150 Hz 到 1500 Hz 左右的所有频率（中低频），其中包含贝斯的泛音以及所有旋律乐器（例如人声、吉他、弦乐、合成器音色等）的基音。歌曲的温暖感和饱满度就蕴藏在这个频段，但过度强调它会产生浑浊的声音。

Commonly the lowest band spans from 16 Hz to 150 Hz (bass) and contains the sub-bass, low rumbling noises, kick-bass and the fundamental notes of the bass instruments. This range is the essential foundation of any song, but too much of it can cause the music to become boomy very quickly. The next band usually covers all frequencies from 150 Hz to around 1500 Hz (lower midrange) and you can find the overtones of the bass in it as well as the fundamental notes of all the melodic instruments: vocals, guitars, strings, pads, and so on. Here lies the warmth and fullness of your song, but over-emphasizing it will produce a muddy sound.





第三频段通常介于 1500 Hz 到 5000 Hz 之间（中高频段），包含所有旋律乐器的泛音，以及大部分踩镲和钹的音色。该频段的声音从最佳的明亮到最差的刺耳尖锐不等。剩下的就是 5000 Hz 到 20000 Hz 之间的“空气”频段（高音）。在这里，你可以找到乐器剩余的泛音以及踩镲、钹和人声的高频部分。这个频段能赋予歌曲一种明亮的声音，但如果音量过大，也会显得嘈杂刺耳。

The third band usually goes from 1500 Hz to 5000 Hz (upper midrange) and contains the overtones of all the melodic instruments as well as much of the hi-hat and cymbal action. The band's sound can range from bright at best to tinny and penetrating at worst. All that's left is the "air" between 5000 Hz and 20000 Hz (treble). Here you'll find the remaining overtones of the instruments and the high end of the hi-hats, cymbals and vocals. This band will give the song a brilliant sound, but can be noisy and piercing if too loud.





多频段压缩器优于单频段压缩器的原因有很多。单频段压缩器启动时，会压缩整个频率范围内的混音。这意味着，例如，低音峰值可能会导致音量正常的较高音符也被抑制，从而使混音听起来更浑浊。而多频段压缩器只会压缩低音峰值，保持较高频段不变，从而保留混音的原始特性。

There are several reasons why a multi-band compressor is superior to its single-band counterpart. When a single-band compressor springs into action, it compresses the mix across the entire frequency spectrum. This means for example that a peaking bass can cause higher notes, that are at an appropriate volume, to be dampened as well, making the mix more boomy. A multi-band compressor on the other hand will only compress the bass peak and leave the higher regions unchanged, keeping the original character of the mix.





更精准的多频段压缩工具还能帮助建立频谱平衡。这对于音频制作新手尤其有用，他们可能不会注意到中低频段的“频率重叠”，而如果没有对各个音轨进行适当的均衡处理，这种情况很容易发生。如果太多乐器在中低频段重叠，混音听起来就会很浑浊。使用设置合适的多频段压缩器可以缓解（但不能完全解决）这个问题，并创建更平衡的频率分布。

The more surgical multi-band compression tool can also help to establish spectral balance. This is especially helpful for audio production beginners who might not notice that there's a "frequency jam" in the lower midrange, something that quickly happens without proper EQing of the individual tracks. With too many instruments overlapping in the lower midrange band, the mix will sound rather muddy. A multi-band compressor with the right settings will alleviate (but not fix) this problem and create a more balanced frequency distribution.





多频段压缩器也可以用作动态均衡器。副歌部分，镲片或歌手的咝音（“s”、“z”和“sh”）是否过大？一种解决方法是用普通均衡器降低5000Hz附近的频率。但遗憾的是，均衡器不仅会抑制副歌中的这些频率，还会抑制歌曲其他部分的频率，就像用锤子修补汽车上的划痕一样。划痕是消失了，但造成的损伤却更大。更好的解决方案是使用多频段压缩器，并选择一个合适的频段（例如5000Hz附近，同时旁通其他三个频段）。这样，只有在副歌部分频率过高时才会抑制该频段，而主歌部分则保持原有的声音。大多数齿音消除器（DeEsser）的工作原理也是如此。

The multi-band compressor can also be used as a dynamic EQ. Are the cymbals or the singer's sibilant consonants ("s", "z" and "sh") getting too loud in the chorus? One way of tackling this problem would be to lower the frequencies around 5000 Hz with a common EQ. But unfortunately, the EQ would dampen these frequencies not only in the chorus, but also in all other parts of the song, sort of like fixing a scratch on your car with a hammer. You got rid of the scratch, but caused a lot more damage in doing it. Applying a multi-band compressor here with a well-chosen band around 5000 Hz (while bypassing the other three bands) would be a much better solution. It will only dampen the band if it gets too loud, that is, in the chorus. The verses get to keep their original sound. Most DeEssers work just like this.





如你所见，多频段压缩器值得深入研究。不要被它复杂的界面吓到，大胆尝试吧。单独测试每个频段，看看它们各自包含哪些功能；加载所有预设，看看它们会如何影响你的音乐；并将你从单频段压缩器中学到的知识应用到多频段压缩器中。我相信你绝对不会后悔。

As you can see, the multi-band compressor is worth studying. Don't be intimidated by its look and start experimenting with it. Solo the bands to see what's in there, load all the presets to see how this will impact your music and apply what you learned about the single-band compressor to the compressors in the multi-band version. I'm sure you won't end up regretting it.





-------------------------------------

-------------------------------------





简而言之——压缩机

In A Nutshell - Compressors





  • 压缩器通过衰减高于阈值的所有声音来降低歌曲的动态范围。压缩比决定了衰减的程度。



  • Compressors reduce the dynamic range of a song by dampening all sounds above the threshold. The ratio determines how pronounced the dampening is.



  • 阈值和比率的适中值可以使歌曲更加饱满温暖，而不会过度限制动态。



  • Moderate values for the threshold and ratio make a song denser and warmer without restricting the dynamics too strongly.



  • 较长的起音和释放时间使压缩机的运行不那么明显，并防止“泵音”。



  • Longer attack and release times make the workings of the compressor less noticeable and prevent "pumping".



  • 并行压缩技术允许你将压缩器部分应用于音轨。



  • The parallel compression technique allows you to apply a compressor partly to a track.



  • 多频段压缩器可以对特定频段进行压缩。它们有助于建立频谱平衡，并可用作动态均衡器。

  • Multi-band compressors allow you to compress isolated frequency bands. They can help to establish spectral balance and act as dynamic equalizers.





-------------------------------------

-------------------------------------









1.2. 限幅器

1.2. Limiters

极端疗法非常适用于严重的疾病——希波克拉底

Extreme remedies are very appropriate for extreme diseases - Hippocrates









限幅器与压缩器密切相关。具体来说，限幅器是一种压缩器，其压缩比最高（∞:1），且启动时间极短。“∞:1”的压缩比意味着所有超过阈值的音符都会被压缩到阈值以下。因此，无论如何，音量都不会超过阈值。需要注意的是，在限幅器中，阈值有时也简称为输出。

Limiters are closely related to compressors. To be specific, a limiter is a compressor with the highest ratio possible (∞:1) and an extremely short attack. A ratio of "infinity-to-one" just means that every note louder than the threshold is pushed down to the threshold. Hence the volume will never go past the threshold, no matter what. Keep in mind that in limiters the threshold is sometimes simply called output.





除了阈值之外，典型的限制器还有哪些参数？由于它本质上是一个压缩器，因此您可以自由选择释放时间。释放时间的常用值约为 200 毫秒，而对于鼓组，释放时间甚至可以低至 0.1 毫秒。通常情况下，使用“自动”功能比手动设置释放时间能获得更好的音质。另一个常见的参数是增益（有时也称为输入）。它决定了混音在经过限制器之前音量增加或减少的幅度。

What other parameters can you find in a typical limiter besides the threshold? Since it is a compressor, you are still free to choose the release. Moderate values for the release are around 200 ms, for drums it can go as low as 0.1 ms. Often a better sound is achieved by using the "auto" function rather than setting the release yourself. Another parameter you commonly find is the gain (sometimes just called input). It specifies by how much the volume of the mix is increased or decreased before it goes through the limiter.

















（Cubase中的限制器）

(Limiter in Cubase)





这种极端的压缩方式有什么意义呢？由于所有响度较高的部分都被压缩到阈值以下，限制器就像一堵“砖墙”。因此，它非常适合防止混音出现削波失真。如果您使用限制器来实现此目的，请确保它是最后一个效果器。如果您先设置了限制器，然后再调整均衡器或添加混响，您的混音仍然可能会出现削波失真。

What's the point of this extreme form of compression? Since all louder parts are pushed down to the threshold, the limiter acts as a "brick wall". It is thus perfect for protecting the mix from clipping. If you are using the limiter for this purpose, make sure that it is the last effect in line. If you set a limiter and then work on the EQ or include reverb after that, your mix could still become subject to clipping.





限幅器的另一个用途是提高歌曲的有效音量。这可以通过选择较大的增益和接近 0 dB 的阈值来实现。下面是一个示例。输入增益设置为 12 dB（因此混音的音量在进入限幅器之前会提高 12 dB），输出阈值设置为 -0.3 dB（因此音量永远不会超过此值）。

Another application of the limiter is to increase the effective volume of a song. This can be done by choosing a large gain and a threshold close to 0 dB. Below you can see an example of this. The gain / input is set to 12 dB (so the volume level of the mix is increased by 12 dB before it goes into the limiter) and the threshold / output set to -0.3 dB (so the volume level will never go past this value).













如果使用得当，这种方法可以显著提升平均音量，同时还能保持宽广的动态范围（这是普通压缩器无法做到的）。但如果过度使用，则会产生刺耳而单调的混音，根本配不上“音乐”二字。找到合适的设置，需要依靠你的耳朵和大脑。

If used wisely, this can increase the average volume considerably while still maintaining the illusion of a large dynamic range (which is what a common compressor is not able to do). If overdone, the result will be a blaring and flat mix that hardly deserves the name music. It is up to your ears and brain to find the right settings.





-------------------------------------

-------------------------------------





简而言之——限制器

In A Nutshell - Limiters





  • 限制器是一种具有极短启动时间和无限比1压缩比的压缩器。



  • Limiters are compressors with an extremely short attack and infinite-to-one ratio.



  • 它们可以用作最终插入效果器，防止削波并提高歌曲的有效音量。

  • They can be used as a final insert to prevent clipping and to increase the effective volume level of a song.





-------------------------------------

-------------------------------------









1.3.均衡器

1.3. Equalizers

问题是你发挥最佳水平的机会——杜克·艾灵顿

A problem is a chance for you to do your best - Duke Ellington









均衡器之于音频工程师，正如螺丝刀之于机械师——是任何工作都必不可少的基本工具。当你开始混音和母带处理之旅时，尽可能多地学习均衡器的相关知识，从宏观概念到细微之处都应有所涉猎。这种学习方式日后必将大有裨益。

Equalizers are to audio engineers as screwdrivers are to mechanics - a fundamental tool you'll need for any job. As you start your journey into mixing and mastering, learn as much as you can about equalization, from the big picture to the nuances. This approach will most certainly pay off later on.





均衡器（EQ）的作用是提升或衰减特定频段，以解决问题或使混音更加出色。如果歌曲过于浑浊，衰减 100 Hz 附近的频段可能会带来显著效果；如果歌曲缺乏温暖感，提升 300 Hz 附近的频段或许正是它所需要的。要正确使用均衡器，您必须能够识别这些问题和不足，确定相应的频段并采取相应的措施。后者需要您了解均衡器的参数，因此本章首先介绍不同类型的均衡器及其参数。

The task of the EQ is to boost or cut a certain frequency region to either solve a problem or make a mix shine. If the song is too boomy, a cut around 100 Hz can do wonders, if it's missing warmth, a boost around 300 Hz might be just what it needs. To properly use the EQ, you have to be able to pick up such problems and shortcomings, identify the corresponding frequency region and take the appropriate action. The latter requires you to know the parameters of your equalizer, which is why we start the chapter by looking at different types of equalizers and the parameters you'll find in them.









  • 图形均衡器

  • Graphic EQs





图形均衡器是一种非常直观的均衡工具。它允许您使用固定中心频率的滑块来指定增益（以分贝为单位的提升或衰减量）。图形均衡器的优点在于易于使用，只需快速查看即可全面了解歌曲频谱的变化情况。但它也有缺点。由于中心频率是固定的，您无法（或至少无法完全）控制提升或衰减的带宽，这限制了其灵活性和精确度。

A very intuitive equalization tool is the graphic EQ. It allows you to specify the gain (the applied boost or cut as measured in decibels) using sliders at fixed center frequencies. The great thing about them is that they are easy to use and that it just takes one quick peek to have the complete picture of how your song's spectrum is modified. But there's also a downside to this. The fact that the center frequencies are fixed and that you have no (or at least not full) control over the bandwidth of the boost or cut takes away some flexibility and precision.













（Cubase 中的 30 段图形均衡器）

(30-Band Graphic EQ in Cubase)





请注意，图形均衡器的定义在于其能够控制固定中心频率的增益，而非如其名称所示，仅仅指其具有图形界面。许多带有图形界面的均衡器并不属于图形均衡器的范畴。

Note that the graphic EQ is defined by having control over the gain at fixed center frequencies and not by the presence of a graphical interface as the name might suggest. There are a lot of EQs with a graphical interface that do not belong in the graphic EQ category.









  • 半参数均衡器

  • Semi-Parametric EQs





半参数均衡器将均衡的概念更进一步。除了增益之外，你还可以自由设置中心频率。它们比图形均衡器或功能更灵活的参数均衡器要少见得多。

Semi-parametric EQs take the equalization concept a step further. Additionally to the gain, you are also free to set the center frequencies. They are much rarer than the graphic EQs or their more flexible brothers, the parametric EQs.













（半参数低音均衡器。上方：频率旋钮，下方：增益旋钮）

(Semi-Parametric Bass EQ. Top: Frequency Knob, Bottom: Gain Knob)









  • 参数方程

  • Parametric EQs





参数均衡器为用户提供尽可能高的精度。除了增益和中心频率之外，它们还允许您通过所谓的Q 值来改变钟形“切口”的带宽。较小的 Q 值会产生较大的带宽（宽钟形曲线），而较大的 Q 值则会产生较小的带宽（窄钟形曲线）。更具体地说，增益或衰减的带宽 B 是中心频率 f 与 Q 值的比值：

Parametric EQs give the user the greatest precision possible. Besides the gain and the center frequency, they allow you to alter the bandwidth of the bell-shaped "incision" via the so-called Q factor. A small Q-value will result in a large bandwidth (broad bell curve), while a large Q-value leads to a small bandwidth (narrow bell curve). To be more specific, the bandwidth B of the boost or cut is the ratio of center frequency f to the Q factor:





B = f / Q

B = f / Q





最佳带宽取决于切分的目的。如果底鼓低音有问题，100 Hz 附近的窄带正态分布曲线应该能很好地解决问题；而如果要在母带处理过程中美化混音，则更适合使用更宽（因此更平滑、更不明显）的正态分布曲线。

Which bandwidth is optimal depends on the purpose of the incision. If there's a problem with the kick bass, a narrow bell curve around 100 Hz should deal with it in a satisfying manner, while for sweetening the mix during mastering a broader (thus smoother and less noticeable) bell curve is much more suitable.













（Cubase 中的 4 段参数均衡器。小 Q 值，高增益提升）

(4-Band Parametric EQ in Cubase. Small Q, High Gain Boost)









  • 货架均衡器

  • Shelving EQs





搁架式均衡器用平台式提升或衰减代替了正态分布曲线。平台的形状由增益、过渡频率和Q值决定。在这种情况下，Q值决定了从初始电平到平台电平的过渡带宽，而不是衰减的幅度。许多参数均衡器（尤其是数字均衡器）都包含搁架式均衡器。

Shelving EQs replace the bell curve with a plateau boost or cut. The form of the plateau is determined by the gain, transition frequency and Q factor. In this case the Q factor specifies the bandwidth of the transition from initial level to plateau level rather than the size of the incision. Many parametric EQs (especially the digital ones) include a shelving EQ.













（Cubase参数均衡器中的小Q值、高增益平台切除）

(Small Q, High Gain Plateau Cut in Cubase's Parametric EQ)









  • 滤波器均衡器

  • Filter EQs





滤波器均衡器（简称滤波器）会对歌曲频谱进行直线衰减。滤除低频的滤波器称为高通滤波器（因为只允许高频通过），而滤除高频的滤波器称为低通滤波器。滤波最重要的参数是截止频率和增益，增益控制衰减的陡峭程度。

Filter EQs (or simply: filters) force a straight-line cut onto a song's spectrum. Filters that cut out low frequencies are called highpass filters (as only high frequencies are allowed to pass), while those that cut out high frequencies are referred to as lowpass filters. The most important parameters for filtering are the cut-off frequency and the gain, which controls the steepness of the cut.













（Cubase 中的过滤器插件）

(Filter Plugin in Cubase)









  • 使用均衡器

  • Using Equalizers





如前所述，均衡器 (EQ) 的用途主要有两个：1) 解决音频中的特定问题，例如低音过重或军鼓过于刺耳；2) 为混音增添色彩。需要注意的是，初学者常犯的错误是选择过高的增益值。如果处理的是相对不错的音轨，增益绝对不应该超过 6 dB（最好是 3 dB）。超过这个值会严重破坏歌曲的频谱平衡，听起来非常不自然。如果低于 6 dB 的增益仍然无法解决问题，那么唯一明智的做法就是回到 录音阶段。

As already mentioned, EQs are used for two purposes: 1) to solve specific problems with the audio such as a boomy bass or an overly aggressive snare and 2) to spice up a mix. It's important to note that it's a common beginner's mistake to choose extreme values for the gain. If you are working with relatively good tracks, there should never be a reason to set the gain higher than 6 dB (or better yet, 3 dB). Anything beyond that will create a severe imbalance in the song's spectrum and sound very artificial. If the problem at hand cannot be fixed with a gain below 6 dB, the only sensible decision is to go back to the recording phase.





在使用均衡器之前，务必先了解混音中各种乐器的频率范围。花些时间记住对你来说最重要的那些频率，因为你会反复用到这些信息。频率范围可以分为基 频区 （乐器的基音所在区域）、 谐波区 （最明显的泛音所在区域）和 空气区 （包含其余的泛音）。空气区未包含在频率表中。它通常从谐波区的末端一直延伸到 16,000 Hz，但很少能被人耳听到。

Before you start working with an EQ, make sure to have an overview over the frequency ranges of the instruments in your mix. Take the time to memorize the ones most important to you, as you will need this information over and over. The range can be divided into the fundamental region (this is where the fundamental notes of the instrument lie), the harmonic region (this is where the most noticeable overtones are) and the air (containing the remaining overtones). The air is not included in the table. It usually spans from the from the end of the harmonic region all the way up to 16.000 Hz and is rarely audible.













1. 同时发出频率在 200 - 300 Hz 之间的铿锵声

1 Also produce a clang between 200 - 300 Hz





2. 包括一个或多个低音提琴

2 Including one or more contra-basses





-------------------------------------

-------------------------------------





背景信息 - 谐波

Background Info - Harmonics





理论上，弹奏钢琴中央C键应该只产生一个频率为523.25赫兹的声波，除此之外别无其他。然而，将这段音频通过频谱分析仪进行分析后，就会发现其中蕴含着更多信息。其他所有乐器也同样如此，从大号到小号，从巴松管到长笛，从低音提琴到小提琴，无一例外。弹奏任何音符，你都会得到一系列不同频率的声波，而不仅仅是一个单一的频率。

In theory, hitting the middle C on a piano should produce a sound wave with a frequency of 523.25 Hz and nothing else. However, running the resulting audio through a spectrum analyzer, it becomes obvious that there's much more going on. This is true for all other instruments, from tubas to trumpets, basoons to flutes, contrabasses to violins. Play any note and you'll get a package of sound waves at different frequencies rather than just one.





首先：这是为什么呢？我们以弦乐器为例。当你拨动琴弦时，它会进入最基本的振动模式：琴弦整体以某个频率 f 上下振动。这就是所谓的基频（或第一谐波）。但不久之后，振动的性质就会发生变化，琴弦进入第二振动模式：琴弦的一半向上振动，另一半向下振动。这是自然发生的，也是琴弦动态特性的一部分。在这个被称为第二谐波的模式下，振动频率会加快到 2f。以此类推，其他振动模式也会出现：频率为 3f 的第三谐波，频率为 4f 的第四谐波，以此类推。

First of all: why is that? Let's focus on stringed instruments. When you pluck the string, it goes into its most basic vibration mode: it moves up and down as a whole at a certain frequency f. This is the so called first harmonic (or fundamental). But shortly after that, the nature of the vibration changes and the string enters a second mode: while one half of the string moves up, the other half moves down. This happens naturally and is just part of the string's dynamics. In this mode, called the second harmonic, the vibration accelerates to a frequency of 2 · f. The story continues in this fashion as other modes of vibration appear: the third harmonic at a frequency 3 · f, the fourth harmonic at 4 · f, and so on.













音符由频率决定。如前所述，钢琴上的中央C应该产生频率为523.25赫兹的声波。它确实会产生这个频率的声波，但这只是第一谐波。随着琴弦持续振动，所有其他谐波也会随之产生，形成泛音。下图展示了弹奏C时会发出哪些音符：

A note is determined by the frequency. As already stated, the middle C on the piano should produce a sound wave with a frequency of 523.25 Hz. And indeed it does produce said sound wave, but it is only the first harmonic. As the string continues to vibrate, all the other harmonics follow, producing overtones. In the image below you can see which notes you'll get when playing a C:













真是个不错的组合！请注意，大三和弦完全包含在前四个泛音中。所以相当于买一个音符，就免费获得一个和弦。你可能会好奇为什么我们似乎听不到这些额外的音符。其实，我们既能听到，又听不到。我们不会刻意去感知泛音，是因为每个泛音的振幅（也就是音量）都比前一个泛音小（当然，这只是个经验法则，任何乐器都会特别强调某些泛音，所以也有例外）。但我可以肯定，当你聆听一个数字合成的音符时，你会感觉少了点什么。它听起来平淡而冰冷。所以，在潜意识里，我们确实能感知到泛音，并且渴望听到它们。

Quite the package! And note that the major chord is fully included within the first four overtones. So it's buy a note, get a chord free. You might wonder why it is that we don't seem to perceive the additional notes. Well, we do and we don't. We don't perceive the overtones consciously because the amplitude, and thus volume, of each harmonic is smaller than the amplitude of the previous one (however, this is a rule of thumb and exceptions are possible as any instrument will emphasize some overtones in particular). But I can assure you that when listening to a digitally produced note, you'll feel that something's missing. It will sound bland and cold. So unconsciously, we do perceive and desire the overtones.





-------------------------------------

-------------------------------------





如果您遇到某个问题，但无法借助上述频率范围表找到合适的频率，请尝试扫频法。使用均衡器进行窄带最大增益提升。移动生成的正态分布曲线，直到问题变得非常明显。显示的中点频率就是您要查找的频率。

If there's a certain problem you'd like to take care of and you don't seem to be able to locate the appropriate frequency with the help of the above frequency range table, try the sweeping technique. Use the EQ to make narrow, maximum gain boost. Move the resulting bell curve through the spectrum until the problem becomes very pronounced. The displayed center frequency is the frequency you where looking for.





扫频技术也是定位和消除共振的绝佳方法。当你扫过乐器的声音时，你会注意到在某些频率上会出现刺耳的嗡嗡声。这些就是共振，通过窄切消除它们，可以使你的音轨达到最佳效果。

The sweeping technique is also an excellent method for locating and eliminating resonances. As you sweep through an instrument's sound, you will notice that at certain frequencies a piercing ringing noise appears. These are resonances and removing them consequently with narrow cuts will bring out the best in your tracks.





在使用均衡器时，尝试在调整增益或衰减之前，先想象一下它的效果。这是一种训练耳朵和思维的绝佳技巧。练习得越多，你就能越快、越精准地判断混音中哪些部分需要提升或衰减才能真正发挥其优势。

Whenever working with the EQ, try to imagine the impact of a boost or cut before you activate it. This is a great technique for training both your ears and mind. The more you'll do it, the quicker and more precise you'll be able to identify where a mix needs a boost or cut to really shine.









  • 快速提示

  • Quick Tips





为了完善均衡器部分，这里提供一些实用的小技巧，或许能帮助你更好地混音和母带处理下一首歌曲。不过，切勿盲目使用。仅在必要时才使用，并务必检查它们是否达到了预期效果。

To complete the section on equalizers, here are a few quick tips that you might find helpful when mixing and mastering your next song. However, don't apply them blindly. Use them only when necessary and be sure to check if they produce the result you were hoping for.





    • 如果 人声难以听清，提升 2 - 6 kHz 之间的频率可能正是您所需要的。



    • If the vocals are hard to understand, a boost between 2 - 6 kHz might be just what you need.



    • 为了让 你的歌声更有亲密感，可以将其通过齿音消除器处理，并添加一个从 10 kHz 开始的高频搁架。

    • For more intimacy in your vocal track, run it through a DeEsser and include a high frequency shelf starting at 10 kHz.

    • 你的 吉他音色听起来很沉闷吗？你应该在录音前更换旧琴弦。为了在后期处理中获得新琴弦的音色，请提升 6-12 kHz 的频段。

    • Does your guitar sound dull? You should have changed your old strings before recording. To get that new string sound in post, boost from 6 - 12 kHz.

    • 如果电吉他的声音不够清晰或过于刺耳，则提升或衰减 2 - 4 kHz 频段。



    • If the electric guitar lacks in sharpness or is too aggressive, boost or cut the region 2 - 4 kHz.



    • 高频部分清晰度不够吗？这可能是吉他的泛音干扰了镲片的声音。将吉他在 6kHz 处提升，同时衰减镲片在该频段的声音；将吉他在 10kHz 处衰减，同时提升镲片在该频段的声音。

    • Is there too little clarity in the high frequency range? This might be a result of the guitar harmonics getting in the way of the cymbals. Boost the guitar at 6 kHz and cut the cymbals there, cut the guitar at 10 kHz and boost the cymbals there.

    • 为了获得清晰的混音，你可能不得不牺牲吉他、军鼓和人声的低频。低切功能可以为贝斯和底鼓腾出空间。

    • You might have to sacrifice the low frequencies of your guitars, snare and vocals to achieve a clear mix. The low-cut leaves space for the bass and kick.

    • 低音和底鼓让你的混音变得浑浊吗？那就试试在 300 Hz 附近进行衰减。

    • Is the bass and kick turning your mix into mud? Then try a cut around 300 Hz.

    • 如果你的混音过于浑浊，可能是贝斯和底鼓之间存在冲突。将底鼓在 80Hz 附近提升，同时将贝斯在该频率处衰减。为了获得更好的分离度，可以将贝斯在 250Hz 附近提升，同时将底鼓在该频率处衰减。

    • If your mix is too boomy, there might be a conflict between the bass and kick. Boost the kick at around 80 Hz and cut the bass there. For an even better separation, boost the bass at 250 Hz and cut the kick there.

    • 低于 40 赫兹的频率，除了暖气、通风、交通等产生的隆隆声之外，几乎没有其他声音……虽然人耳听不到，但它仍然占据着宝贵的动态空间。毫不留情地去除它，一个都不要留。

    • Below 40 Hz, there's nothing except rumbling from heating, ventilation, traffic, etc ... It might not be audible, but it still uses up precious dynamic space. Get rid of it mercilessly, don't leave survivors.

    • 我们的耳朵对 3-4 kHz 频段最为敏感。因此，如果你想让某种乐器更加突出，就应该在这个频段提升它的频率。同时，削弱同一频段内其他乐器的音量，可以产生更显著的效果。

    • Our ears are most sensitive between 3 - 4 kHz. So if you want to make an instrument stand out, this is where to boost it. Cut conflicting instruments in the same range for an even more pronounced effect.





    正如你所看到的，很多技巧都侧重于创造空间。这是混音的核心部分。如果你想要清晰的混音，就必须做出取舍。你有很多乐器，但只有一个低频频段和一个 3-4 kHz 的频段。想想哪些乐器应该占据这些高频段，然后相应地进行均衡。

    As you noticed, a lot of these tips focus on making space. This is a very central part of mixing. If you want a clear mix, you have to make sacrifices. You have a lot of instruments, but only one bass band and only one 3 - 4 kHz range. Think about which instruments get these top spots and EQ accordingly.

    -------------------------------------





    简而言之——均衡器

    In A Nutshell - Equalizers





    • 均衡器可以让你提升或衰减特定频段，用于单个乐器或整个混音。



    • Equalizers allow you to boost or cut specific frequency bands for individual instruments or an entire mix.



    • 要正确使用均衡器，需要熟悉音乐中各种乐器的频率范围。

    • To be able to use EQs properly, get familiar with the frequency ranges of the instruments in your music.

    • 要确定某个问题所在的频率，可以使用扫频技术。



    • To identify at which frequency a certain problem is located, use the sweeping technique.



    • 在进行任何音量增强或减弱操作之前，务必先想象一下其效果。这对你的耳朵来说是很好的训练。

    • Always imagine the impact of your boost or cut before applying it. This is great training for your ears.

    • 使用均衡器消除共振和低频隆隆声，并在某些频段腾出空间。后者对于清晰的混音至关重要。

    • Use the EQ to get rid of resonances and low-end rumbling as well as to make space in certain bands. The latter is vital for a clear mix.

    1.4 混响和延迟

    1.4. Reverb and Delay

    你的精神力量对我不起作用，小子——贾巴·赫特

    Your mind powers will not work on me, boy - Jabba the Hutt









    混响是音频制作中最常用（也最常被误用）的效果器之一。它可以让平淡的录音听起来更加饱满，并能很好地将混音融合在一起。然而，过多的混响会让原本不错的混音变得浑浊或轰鸣——这是初学者常犯的错误。尽量避免落入这个陷阱。

    Reverb is among the most often used (and misused) effects in audio production. It can make a flat recording sound grand and really glue a mix together. Too much of it however will turn a good mix into a muddy or boomy mess - a typical beginner's mistake. Try your best to avoid this trap.









    • 基础知识

    • Basics





    在深入探讨之前，我们先来明确一下混响和延迟的区别。从物理角度来看，它们本质上是一回事，都是声波从墙壁或其他障碍物反射的结果。区别在于我们的大脑如何处理声音。

    Before we go any further, let's make sure we understand the difference between reverb and delay. From a physical point of view, they are one and the same, that is, a result of sound waves being reflected from walls or other barriers. The difference rather comes from how our brain processes sound.





    假设你身处一个房间，打了个响指发出声音。你产生的声波会​​传播到墙壁，然后反射回来。由于声波传播速度极快——大约每秒330米，或每毫秒33厘米（约一英尺），因此这个过程发生得非常快。所以在一个普通大小的卧室里，第一次反射声波会在短短5毫秒内到达你耳中。声波会在房间内不断来回传播并逐渐衰减。

    Suppose you are in a room and produce a sound by snapping your fingers. The sound waves you created travel to the walls and are reflected back to you. This happens in a very short time span as sound waves travel very fast - with roughly 330 meters per second or 33 centimeters (circa one foot) per millisecond. So in a commonly sized bedroom the first reflection will reach you after only 5 milliseconds. The sound waves keep on traveling back and forth within the room while dissipating.





    我们的大脑有一种奇特的处理方式，专门处理声音发出后最初30毫秒内到达的反射声。大脑不会清晰地感知这些早期反射声，而是将它们与声源混合在一起。它甚至会告诉你，这些反射声来自与原始声音相同的位置。因此，在我们听来，原始声音似乎会持续一段时间。这种“绝地武士般的思维技巧”被称为混响（或厅堂效应）。

    Our brain has a curious way of processing reflections that arrive within the first 30 milliseconds after producing the sound. Instead of distinctly perceiving those early reflections, the brain blends them with the sound source. It will even tell you that these reflections came from the same place as the original sound. So to us it seems that the original sound persist for a while. This Jedi mind-trick is called reverb (or hall).













    （上图：干军鼓声，下图：带混响的军鼓声）

    (Top: Dry Snare, Bottom: Snare with Reverb)





    最初30毫秒后到达你所在位置的反射声会被感知为来自墙壁的独立反射声。这种现象被称为延迟（或回声）。一个很好的例子是，你的“你好”被山体反射回来。这种反射声听起来像是从山体发出的独立声音，不会与你最初的“你好”混杂在一起。

    The reflections that arrive at your location after the initial 30 milliseconds are perceived as distinct reflections coming from the walls. They go by the name delay (or echo). A good example is a mountain throwing back your "hello". The reflection is heard as a distinct sound originating from the mountain and is not blended with your original "hello".













    （上图：干军鼓声，下图：加延迟的军鼓声）

    (Top: Dry Snare, Bottom: Snare with Delay)









    • 混响时间

    • Reverb Time





    混响插件中常见的参数有哪些？市面上的混响插件种类繁多，有些非常相似，有些则独具特色。但所有插件都会包含一个名为“混响时间”（也称为衰减或 RT60）的参数。它指定混响衰减 60 dB 所需的时间，简而言之，就是混响持续的时间。显然，这个数值与房间的大小有关。房间越大，混响时间就越长。

    What are the common parameters you find in a reverb plugin? There's a great variety of reverb plugins out there, some very similar, others very unique. But all will feature a parameter called reverb time (also called decay or RT60). It specifies the time it takes the reverberation to decay by 60 dB or in short: how long the reverb persists. Obviously this quantity is related to the size of a room. The bigger it is, the longer the reverb time will be.





    19世纪末，华莱士·克莱门特·萨宾在哈佛大学对混响时间进行了实证研究，并推导出了一个方便的近似公式。以下是考虑空气损耗的改进版本：

    At the end of the 19th century, Wallace Clement Sabine empirically studied the reverb time at Harvard University and derived a handy approximation formula for it. Here is a modified version of it that takes into account air dissipation:









    其中 T 为混响时间（秒），V 为房间体积（立方米），A 为房间表面积（平方米）。普通砖墙和石膏墙的吸声系数约为 a = 0.03，木材约为 a = 0.3，而吸声瓷砖的吸声系数可高达 a = 0.8。空气吸声系数在 50% 湿度下约为 b = 0.02。但请注意，该公式仅适用于空房间。房间内如有设备和人员等吸声物，会显著缩短混响时间（没错，我刚才就说你是吸声物，你能拿我怎么样？）。

    with T being the reverb time in seconds, V the room's volume in cubic-meters and A the surface area of the room in square-meters. For common brickwork and plaster walls the absorption coefficient is about a = 0.03, for wood a = 0.3 and for acoustic tiles it can go as high as a = 0.8. As for the air absorption coefficient, it is roughly b = 0.02 at 50 % humidity. Keep in mind though that the formula is only valid for empty rooms. Having sound absorbers such as equipment and people in a room can greatly reduce the reverb time (that's right, I just called you a sound absorber, what are you gonna do about it?).













    （空旷矩形房间内混响时间随音量的变化）

    (Variation Of Reverb Time With Volume For Empty, Rectangular Rooms)





    如果你不喜欢公式，别担心。虽然了解公式很有用，但对于音乐制作来说并非必不可少。只需记住一些混响时间的参考值：小型家庭房间为 0.5 秒，教堂为 1 秒，音乐厅为 1.5 秒，小型体育馆为 2 秒，大型体育馆为 2.5 秒。

    If you don't like formulas, don't worry. The formula, while good to know, is not essential for music production. Just keep in mind some reference values for the reverb time: 0.5 s for small rooms in a home, 1 s for churches, 1.5 s for concert halls, 2 s for small arenas and 2.5 s for large arenas.













    （Cubase中的混响插件）

    (Reverb Plugin in Cubase)









    • 其他混响参数

    • Other Reverb Parameters





    几乎所有混响插件都有一个共同的参数：预延迟。它指的是声音产生到第一次反射到达之间的时间间隔。计算方法非常简单。如果最近的墙壁距离声源 d 米，那么预延迟 t（以毫秒为单位）大致为：

    Another parameter that is found in almost all reverb plugins is the pre-delay. It is the time span between the sound being created and the arrival of the first reflection. Calculating it is very simple. If the closest wall is at a distance of d meters, then the pre-delay t in milliseconds is roughly:





    t = 6 · d

    t = 6 · d





    与混响时间一样，预延迟通常会随着房间大小的增加而增加。因此，最好将预延迟设置得与混响时间大致成比例。假设您位于房间中央，典型的预延迟值在家庭小房间约为 20 毫秒，教堂约为 60 毫秒，音乐厅约为 120 毫秒，小型体育馆约为 200 毫秒，大型体育馆约为 250 毫秒。

    Just like the reverb time, the pre-delay generally grows with the size of the room. Hence, it's a good idea to set the pre-delay in a more or less proportional fashion to the reverb time. Assuming you are in the middle of the room, typical pre-delays are around 20 ms for small rooms in a home, 60 ms for a church, 120 ms for a concert hall, 200 ms for a small arena and 250 ms for a large arena.





    从物理角度来看，将较短的预延迟和较长的混响时间结合起来也是可行的。例如，在长长的隧道中或大房间的墙壁附近，就会出现这种组合。在这两种情况下，第一次反射都会很快返回，而房间的大小则保证了较长的混响时间。

    Combining a small pre-delay and large reverb time is also possible from a physical point of view. This combination occurs for example in a long tunnel or near a wall in a large room. In both cases the first reflection will come back quickly, while the size of the room guarantees a long reverb time.





    混响插件中另一个常见的重要参数是 扩散（diffuse）。假设你身处一栋房子里，有两个大小相同的房间。这两个房间唯一的区别在于表面纹理：一个房间的表面非常光滑，而另一个房间的表面则非常粗糙。由于房间大小相同，混响时间和预延迟在两个房间中也相同。但即便如此，混响听起来却截然不同。一个房间光滑的表面会产生更硬、更明显的混响，而另一个房间粗糙的表面则会产生更温暖、更柔和的混响。扩散参数可以模拟这种情况。将其设置为接近 0% 可获得光滑表面（硬混响），接近 100% 可获得粗糙表面（温暖混响）。

    Another important parameter you can commonly find in reverb plugins is diffusion. Suppose you are in a house with two rooms of identical size. The rooms only differ in surface texture: while one room has a perfectly smooth surface, the surface of the other room is very rough. Because of the equal size, the reverb time and pre-delay will be the same in both rooms. But despite that, the reverb will sound different. While the smooth surface in the one room creates a harder and more noticeable reverb, the rough surface in the other room will spawn a warmer and more subtle reverb. The diffusion parameter allows you to simulate this situation. Set it close to 0 % for a smooth surface (hard reverb) and close to 100 % for a rough surface (warm reverb).





    参数 混合也非常有用。通过它，您可以指定输出中湿信号（即经过混响插件处理的信号）的比例。如果接近 0%，混响几乎听不到；而 100% 的值则会提供完整的混响效果。选择数值时，请记住“少即是多”的原则。10% 左右的混合比例通常就足够了（如果混响作为插入效果器使用——稍后会详细介绍）。

    Also very helpful is the parameter mix. With it you specify how much of the wet signal, that is, the signal that was processed by the reverb plugin, you'd like to have in the output. If it's close to 0 % the reverb will hardly be noticeable, while a value of 100 % gives you the full dose of reverb. When choosing your value, don't forget the saying "less is more". A mix of around 10 % is often quite sufficient (if the reverb is used as an insert - more on that later).





    混响插件里还会包含哪些功能？这方面的差异很大。许多插件还会内置 滤波器 ，这并非没有道理。在混响插件处理信号之前，先对低频和高频进行衰减是非常有意义的。低频音频内容很容易让混音变得浑浊不堪，尤其是在经过混响插件处理之后。而混响中过多的高频听起来则非常不自然。这是为什么呢？空气在传播声波时，对高频的衰减远强于低频。因此，当来回反射的声音 到达你耳中时，空气已经吸收了大部分高频成分。所以，自然混响通常缺乏高频成分。

    What else will there be in the reverb plugin? This can vary greatly. Many plugins also a include a filter and this for good reasons. Dampening low and high frequencies before having the reverb plugin process your signal makes a lot of sense. Low frequency audio content can easily make a mix boomy and muddy when run through a reverb plugin. And having a lot of high frequencies in your reverb sounds very unnatural. Why is that? Air has the habit of dampening high frequencies much more strongly than low frequencies as it transmits sound waves. So when the sound that was reflected back and forth reaches you, the air has already taken out a lot of the high frequencies. Hence, natural reverb lacks in high frequency content.





    滤波器通常由截止频率和阻尼参数控制。截止频率参数决定了开始衰减频谱的频率（低切通常约为 50 Hz，高切通常约为 7000 Hz）。在 Cubase 的 Roomworks 插件中，滤波器的截止频率参数位于左侧顶部。阻尼参数（通常以增益旋钮的形式）指定了衰减的程度。适中的阻尼值约为 -4 dB。在 Roomworks 插件中，阻尼参数位于左侧底部。

    The filters are usually controlled by a cut-off and dampening parameter. The cut-off parameter determines at what frequency to start dampening the spectrum (usually somewhere around 50 Hz for the low cut and 7000 Hz for the high cut). In Cubase's Roomworks plugin the cut-off parameters for the filters can be found on the left side at the top. The dampening parameter, usually in form of a gain knob, specifies how pronounced the cut is. Moderate values are around - 4 dB. In the Roomworks plugin the dampening parameters are located on the left side at the bottom.









    • 延迟参数

    • Delay Parameters













    （Cubase 中的单声道延迟插件）

    (Mono Delay Plugin in Cubase)





    延迟插件最重要的参数是延迟时间，也就是两次反射之间的时间间隔，单位为毫秒。需要注意的是，虽然对于压缩器和混响插件来说，根据歌曲节奏调整时间参数是获得更完美音质的巧妙方法，但对于延迟插件来说，谨慎选择至关重要。不同步的延迟会让混音变得一团糟，因此大多数延迟插件都配备了同步功能，你应该充分利用它。

    The most important parameter in delay plugins is the delay, that is, the time between reflections in milliseconds. Note that while for compressors and reverb plugins setting the temporal parameters to fit the rhythm of your song is a neat trick to achieve a more perfect sound, in case of delay making a careful choice is essential. An out-of-sync delay can turn a mix into a mess, which is why most delay plugins feature a sync function that you should make use of.





    反馈参数控制反射的数量和强度。接近 0% 的值只会产生一个明显的反射（后续反射衰减太快，听不到），而接近 100% 的值会在每个音符后添加一长串明显的反射。

    The feedback parameter controls the number of reflections as well as their intensity. A value close to 0 % will only produce one noticeable reflection (the following reflections decay too quickly to be heard), while a value close to 100 % will add a long line of noticeable reflections to each note.









    • 使用混响和延迟

    • Using Reverb And Delay





    在混音中使用混响和延迟的可能性无穷无尽。大胆尝试吧！除了需要注意的几点之外，并没有绝对的对错之分。换句话说：只要听起来好听，就是好听的。那么需要注意什么呢？首先，对低频音频素材使用混响或延迟通常会导致混音听起来暗沉浑浊。因此，在给贝斯、底鼓、大提琴、中提琴和吉他添加这些效果时，务必注意这一点。

    The possibilities of using reverb and delay in your mix are endless. Be bold and experiment with them. Besides a few things to keep in mind, there's no right and wrong. In other words: if it sounds good, it is good. What's to keep in mind? For one, reverb or delay on low frequency audio content often leads to a dark and boomy mix. Watch out for that when adding them to the bass, kick, cello, viola and guitar.





    如果你的歌曲中吉他部分需要较重的混响，请务必事先削减低频，可以使用均衡器或混响插件自带的滤波器。如果低频削减后吉他独奏听起来太单薄，不用担心。关键不在于独奏效果，而在于它在混音中的整体表现。至于贝斯，几乎总是最好不要使用混响。如果你想要更饱满的贝斯音色，不妨试试添加一些失真效果。

    If having a relatively heavy reverb on the guitar is important for your song, make sure to cut the low frequencies beforehand, either with the EQ or the filter included in the reverb plugin. If the guitar sounds too thin in solo after the low cut, don't worry. It's not about how it sounds solo, it's all about how it sounds within the mix. As for the bass, it's almost always better off with very little or no reverb. If you'd like to have a more vivid bass, why not add some distortion instead?





    高频部分也可能出现问题，尤其是在人声轨道上。过重的混响或延迟会让齿音更加刺耳。考虑到人声在歌曲中总是占据主导地位，这可能会毁掉原本很棒的混音。因此，如果你想给歌声添加明显的混响（这通常是个好主意），请务必在混响插件之前添加一个齿音消除器（DeEsser）。

    Problems can also occur in the high frequency range, especially in case of vocal tracks. A heavy reverb or delay can make sibilant consonants even more problematic. Considering that the vocals are always at the front of a song, this can ruin an otherwise great mix. So if you want to put a noticeable reverb on the vocals (which is generally a good idea), make sure to place a DeEsser before the reverb plugin.





    一个更显而易见的要点是，混音中大部分音轨应该使用同一个混响室（或类似的房间）。对于人声或电吉他等特定元素，你可以也应该打破这个规则。没有什么比在小房间混响中呈现一段气势磅礴的教堂吉他独奏更震撼的了——不妨一试。

    A more obvious point that you should keep in mind is to use the same reverb room (or comparable rooms) for the majority of the tracks in your mix. For specific elements such as the vocals or electric guitar you can and should deviate from this rule. There's nothing more powerful than an epic cathedral guitar solo over a small room mix - try it out.





    混响和延迟是营造混音深度感的绝佳工具。因此，在使用它们之前，请先考虑哪些音轨离听众较近，哪些音轨离听众较远。乐器越靠后，混音参数的值就应该越高。您可以通过对后方乐器进行更明显的高频衰减来增强这种深度感（记住，声音在空气中传播的距离越远，高频成分损失就越多）。流行/摇滚歌曲的典型设置是：人声和独奏乐器在前，吉他和鼓在中，其他所有乐器（尤其是弦乐和合成器音色）在后。

    Reverb and delay are great tools to create a sense of depth in your mix. So before you start applying them, think about which of your tracks are close and which are far from the audience. The farther back an instrument is, the higher the value of the mix parameter should be. You can boost this sense of depth by making a more pointed high cut for the instruments in the back (remember, if sound travels a greater distance in air, it will lose more of the high frequency content). A typical set-up for a pop / rock song is: vocals and solo instruments in the front, guitars and drums in the middle, everything else in the back (especially strings and pads).









    • 插入还是发送？

    • Insert or Send?





    插入效果是指直接添加到音轨路径中的任何效果。这是最直观的音轨添加效果的方式，如果您是新手，可能之前一直都只使用插入效果。您只需打开音轨的设置并添加效果即可。就这么简单。对于很多用途来说，这已经足够了。

    An insert effect is any effect that is placed directly into the path of one track. This is the most intuitive way of putting an effect on a track and if you're a beginner you've probably been only using insert effects up to now. You simply open the track's settings and include the effect. Done and done. For many purposes, this is quite sufficient.













    （使用插入效果器的信号路径）

    (Signal Paths Using Insert-Effects)





    将效果器作为发送通道意味着走一条捷径。我们不将效果器直接包含在音轨的路径中，而是将音轨信号发送到效果器，然后再由效果器发送到输出。这样，原始信号和经过效果器插件处理后的信号就被分离了。最终，两者都会被发送到输出，您可以通过相应的音量推子来控制输出中每种信号的比例。例如，您无需提高混音参数来增加音轨的混响，只需提高单独效果器通道的音量即可。

    Using an effect as a send means making a short a detour. Instead of including the effect in the track's path, we send the signal of the track to the effect, which is then sent to the output. So the original signal and the signal processed by the effect plugin are separated. Both are ultimately send to the output and with the respective volume faders you can determine how much of each you'd like to have in the output. Instead of turning up the mix parameter to get more reverb on a track, you turn up the volume of the separate effect channel.













    （使用发送效果的信号路径）

    (Signal Paths Using A Send-Effect)





    这一切究竟有何意义？一方面，从经济角度来看。将十个音轨路由到独立的效果通道，比在每个音轨上单独插入同一个混响效果器要节省大量的计算资源。你的电脑会感谢你的。更重要的是，现在你可以自由地在效果器上叠加效果。你可以在不改变原始信号的情况下，为混响或延迟添加柔和的合唱效果。你还可以将音轨声像定位到一侧，而将延迟声像定位到另一侧——这真是一个巧妙的设计。它开启了音乐制作的全新世界。

    What's the point of all this hassle? On the one hand there's the economic side of it. Routing ten tracks to the separate effect channel requires a lot less computing power than inserting one and the same reverb on all ten tracks individually. Your computer will thank you for that. More importantly, you are now free to put effects on your effect. You can spice up the reverb or delay with a soft chorus without altering the original signal. You can also pan the track to one side and its delay to the other - a nice touch. It opens up a whole new world of music production.





    在 Cubase 中使用发送效果的方法如下：首先创建一个 FX 通道，为其命名，然后将所需的效果插入到该通道中。

    This is how you can use send effects in Cubase: First create an FX channel, name it appropriately and insert the desired effect into this channel.

















    （在 Cubase 中创建 FX 通道）

    (Creating an FX Channel in Cubase)





    现在找到你想发送到效果器通道的音轨，打开它的设置（也就是点击“e”按钮）。通常情况下，效果器会放在均衡器的左侧。但这次请将注意力转移到右侧。在那里你可以插入你创建的效果器通道。

    Now go to the track that you would like to send to the FX channel and open its settings (that is, click on the "e" button). The left side of the EQ is where you usually place the effects. But this time turn your attention to the right side. There you can insert the FX channel you created.













    （将乐器信号发送到效果器通道）

    (Sending an Instrument to the FX channel)





    请务必将效果通道名称下方的滑块向右移动，否则音轨信号将无法到达效果通道。现在您应该能够通过效果通道听到混响效果了。

    Make sure to move the slider below the FX channel's name to the right, otherwise the track's signal will not reach the FX channel. Now you should be able to hear the reverb via the FX channel.













    （滑块向右移动，预推子功能已激活）

    (Slider Moved to the Right, Pre-Fader Function Activated)





    您可能会注意到，在乐器设置中，FX通道名称的正上方有一个按钮，用于切换推子后和推子前发送模式，默认设置为推子后发送。这两者有什么区别呢？在推子后发送模式下，效果通道的输出会与乐器的输出成比例变化。因此，如果您降低乐器的音量，FX通道的音量也会相应降低。换句话说：在这种情况下，干湿信号的比例得以保持。

    You might notice that right above the FX channel's name in the instrument settings there is a button to switch between post-fader and pre-fader, with post-fader being the default. What's the difference? In a post-fader send the output of the effect channel will vary in a proportional fashion to the output of the instrument. So if you decrease the instrument's volume level, the same will happen to the FX channel. In other words: the ratio of dry-to-wet is preserved in this case.





    选择推子前效果器，即可完全控制效果通道的输出。即使将乐器音量推子推到最低（-∞ ）， 效果通道的输出也不会改变。如果您只想听处理后的信号，而不想听原始信号，此功能非常有用。

    When choosing pre-fader you get full control over the output of the effect channel. Even when moving the instrument's volume fader all the way down to -∞, the output of the FX channel will remain unchanged. This is useful if you only want to listen to the processed signal and not the original signal that created it.

    -------------------------------------





    简而言之——混响和延迟

    In A Nutshell - Reverb And Delay





    • 混响和延迟之间的区别源于我们大脑处理声音的方式。



    • The difference between reverb and delay is a result of how our brain processes sound.



    • 混响（= 混响）是由声波反射与原始声音混合而成，而延迟（= 回声）则是由清晰可辨的反射组成。



    • Reverb (= hall) is made up of sound wave reflections that are blended with the original sound, while delay (= echo) consists of distinctly perceived reflections.



    • 混响时间衡量的是声音持续的时间长短。房间越大，混响时间越长。卧室通常为0.5秒，音乐厅通常为1.5秒。



    • The reverb time is a measure of how long the sound persists. The larger the room, the longer the reverb time. 0.5 s for bedrooms, 1.5 s for concert halls.



    • 预延迟时间告诉我们第一次反射光到达我们这里需要多长时间。我们离反射墙越远，预延迟时间就越长。



    • The pre-delay tells us how long it takes the first reflection to reach us. The farther we are from a reflecting wall, the longer the pre-delay.



    • 扩散参数模拟表面粗糙度。对于粗糙的表面（从而产生温暖而柔和的混响），请将其设置为接近 100%。



    • The diffusion parameter simulates surface roughness. For a rough surface (and thus warm and subtle reverb) set it close to 100 %.



    • 不要使用过多的混响或延迟。削减低频以避免混音浑浊，削减高频以获得自然的声音。



    • Don't use too much reverb or delay. Cut the low frequencies to avoid a muddy mix, cut the high frequencies to achieve a natural sound.



    • 延迟是指两次反射之间的时间。通常需要将其与歌曲的节奏同步。



    • Delay is the time between two reflections. It is usually necessary to synchronize it with your song's rhythm.



    • 使用混响和延迟来营造深度感。人声和独奏乐器放在前面，吉他和鼓放在中间，其他乐器放在后面。

    • Use reverb and delay to create a sense of depth. Vocals and solo instruments in the front, guitars and drums in the middle, everything else in the back.

    1.5. 盖茨

    1.5. Gates

    你！不！能！过！——灰袍甘道夫

    You! Shall! Not! Pass! - Gandalf the Grey









    噪声门是音频工程师的垃圾处理工具。它们并不惊艳，但却极其有用。当音轨本应静音却并非如此时，噪声门就能解决这个问题。例如，假设你正在录制人声。在人声停顿期间，许多背景噪音会变得清晰可闻：隆隆声、沉重的呼吸声、清嗓声等等……虽然这些噪音并不特别大，但仍然会让混音变得杂乱无章。这对于重金属音乐来说或许可以接受，但对于流行、摇滚或古典音乐来说就不太合适了。这时，噪声门就派上用场了。

    Gates are the audio engineer's waste disposal tool. They are not spectacular, but extremely useful. When a track is supposed to be silent but it is not, the (noise) gate will take care of it. Suppose for example that you are recording a vocal track. During pauses, a lot of background noises become audible: rumbling, heavy breathing, clearing the throat, etc ... While not particularly loud, they can still make a mix dirty. This might be fine for heavy metal, but not so much for pop, rock or classical music. Here's where the gate comes in.





    当音轨的音量低于阈值时，门限器会将其完全静音。一旦音量达到阈值，门限器就会失效，允许音频通过。下图展示了门限器的工作原理。原始音频位于顶部，经过门限处理的音频位于底部。

    A gate silences a track completely as long as its volume level is below a threshold. Once the threshold is reached, the gate becomes inactive and lets the audio pass. In the image below you can see what the workings of a gate look like. The original audio is at the top, the gated audio at the bottom.













    歌手开始演唱之前音轨中的噪音现在已经消失了。请注意，阈值必须谨慎选择。如果阈值太低，可能会有噪音漏进来；如果阈值太高，噪声门可能会滤除重要的音频信号。您需要通过反复试验找到合适的阈值。

    The noise that was in the track before the singer springs into action is now gone. Note that the threshold has to be chosen carefully. If it's too low, there is the danger of some noise coming through, if it's too high, the gate might cut out relevant audio signals. You have to find the right value by trial and error.













    （Cubase 中的噪声门）

    (The Noise Gate in Cubase)





    其他参数呢？和压缩器一样，噪声门通常也需要设置启动时间和释放时间。启动时间决定了噪声门打开所需的时间。对于鼓和吉他来说，1毫秒左右的极短启动时间就足够了。但对于人声来说，如此低的启动时间可能会导致静音部分过于突兀地结束。为了避免这种情况，建议主音人声的启动时间接近10毫秒，伴唱人声接近50毫秒。释放时间的典型值在100到300毫秒之间。

    What about the other parameters? Just like compressors, gates usually feature attack and release. The attack specifies how long it takes the gate to open. For drums and guitars very short attacks of around 1 ms work just fine. In case of vocals however, such a low value could lead to an overly abrupt end to the silence. To avoid this, choose a value closer to 10 ms for the lead and 50 ms for the backings. Typical values for the release are anywhere between 100 and 300 ms.





    至于保持时间，它是指门控器保持打开或关闭的最短持续时间。某些信号和阈值可能会导致门控器快速连续地频繁打开和关闭。保持功能通过强制门控器在当前状态保持一段时间来缓解这种情况。作为参考，鼓和吉他可以使用 100 毫秒，人声可以使用 250 毫秒。

    As for the hold, it is the minimum duration the gate stays open or closed. Some signals and thresholds might cause the gate to nervously open and close in rapid succession. The hold function brings calm into this by forcing the gate to remain in its current state for a while. As a reference, you can use 100 ms for drums and guitars and 250 ms for vocals.





    -------------------------------------

    -------------------------------------





    简而言之——盖茨

    In A Nutshell - Gates





    • 门控装置会在轨道应该静音的时候将其静音。



    • Gates silence a track when it's supposed to be silent.



    • 将阈值设置为一个可以消除背景噪音但保留音乐的值。

    • Set the threshold to a value that mutes the background gibberish, but leaves the music intact.
