    -------------------------------------









    1.6. 合唱

    1.6. Chorus

    在一个完美的世界里，不完美才是王道——佚名

    In a perfect world, imperfection is king - Anonymous









    合唱效果器（以及其他调制效果器，例如镶边、相位和颤音）在20世纪60年代迷幻音乐席卷全球时迅速流行起来。尽管在接下来的几十年里，音乐产业回归了更为务实的曲风，但这些调制效果器仍然被广泛使用。合唱效果器至今仍是音乐制作中最常用的效果器之一，尽管如今它的运用方式更加微妙。

    Chorus (as well as other modulation effects such as flanger, phaser and tremolo) gained in popularity when a wave of psychedelic music swept across the globe in the sixties. While the music industry went back to more pragmatic tunes in the following decades, the modulation effects remained in use. Chorus is still among the most often used effects in music production, though today it is applied in a much more subtle manner.









    • 为什么选择合唱？

    • Why Chorus?





    在了解插件如何实现合唱效果之前，我们先来看看整体情况。假设你录制了一段小提琴独奏，然后多次复制这段音轨。最终效果听起来会像是由几位不同的小提琴手演奏的小提琴组吗？很遗憾，不会。它听起来就像是一段独奏音轨被多次复制，这毫无意义。那么，我们有什么办法能让它听起来更像一个真实的小提琴组呢？

    Before we look at how plugins create the chorus effect, let's take a look at the big picture. Suppose you record a solo violin and duplicate this track several times. Will the result sound like a violin section with several different violin players? No, unfortunately not. It will just sound like a solo track copied several times, which is not helpful. Is there any way we can get it to sound more like a real violin section?





    这就是合唱效果器的用途。将其插入小提琴独奏音轨，就能营造出多把小提琴同时演奏的效果，而不仅仅是一把。因此，合唱效果器模拟了合唱团的演奏 ，同时还能产生丰富、浑厚而温暖的声音 。难怪它是音频工程师的最爱。

    This is what the chorus effect is for. Inserting it into the solo violin track will give the impression of having multiple violins playing rather than just one. So the chorus effect simulates a choir and produces a rich, thick and warm sound while doing so. No wonder it's the audio engineer's darling.









    • 工作原理

    • How It Works





    假设我们将一段复制的小提琴音轨混音并播放。为什么听起来不像两个不同的小提琴手演奏？问题在于复制的音轨与原音轨完美契合，它们在任何时刻都保持着完全相同的节奏和音高，而两个真正的小提琴手在节奏和音高上总会存在细微的差别。因此，为了营造出多个演奏者的感觉，我们需要对复制的音轨进行修改，以模拟这种自然的节奏和音高变化。

    Suppose we mix a duplicate to a solo violin track and hit play. Why does the result not sound like two different violin players? The problem is that the duplicate fits the original track perfectly, they have exactly the same tempo and pitch at any time, while two real violin players would always be slightly off in timing and pitch. So to give the impression of more than one player, we need to modify the duplicate in a way that simulates this natural variation in timing and pitch.





    合唱插件首先会复制音轨，并给副本添加延迟（并非回声，而是改变副本的起始点）。为了模拟时序变化，延迟量会随时间变化。用专业的音频工程术语来说：延迟时间由低频振荡器 (LFO) 调制。合唱延迟的典型值约为 20 毫秒，并有正负 5 毫秒的波动。这种调制的一个副作用是音高也会随时间变化，从而进一步营造出时序和音高不完美的错觉。

    Chorus plugins first create a duplicate of the track and "equip" the duplicate with a delay (not in the sense of echo, but in the sense of shifting the duplicate's starting point). To simulate variations in timing, the amount of delay varies with time. In fancy audio engineering terms: the delay time is modulated with an LFO, short for low frequency oscillator. A typical value for a chorus delay is around 20 milliseconds with variations of plus/minus 5 milliseconds. One side-effect of the modulation is that the pitch also varies with time, which completes the illusion of imperfect timing and pitch.









    • 参数

    • The Parameters













    （Cubase 中的基础合唱插件）

    (Basic Chorus Plugin in Cubase)





    几乎所有合唱插件都有一个参数叫做速率（或速度）。它决定了重复音的延迟时间（从而音高）变化的频率。一般来说，速率越高，合唱效果越明显。如果想要更柔和的增厚效果，低于 0.4 Hz 的速率效果最佳。许多插件还带有同步功能，可以使延迟时间和音高变化与歌曲的节奏保持一致。这很实用，但并非必不可少，因为我们通常都能听到合唱团和弦乐部分中自然出现的不同步的合唱效果。

    A parameter found in almost all chorus plugins is the rate (or speed). It determines at what frequency the delay time, and thus pitch, of the duplicate varies. In general it holds true that the higher the rate, the more pronounced the chorus effect is. For a subtle thickening, rates below 0.4 Hz work best. Many plugins also feature a sync-function to bring the delay time and pitch variations in line with the song's rhythm. This is neat, but not essential as we are used to hearing (natural) out-of-sync chorus effects in choirs and string sections.





    参数“延迟” （取决于插件，可以是初始延迟时间或平均延迟时间）和“宽度”（衡量延迟时间变化幅度）可以让你更好地控制振荡。同样，我们可以遵循同样的经验法则：数值越高，合唱效果越强。为了使效果保持在背景中，请将“宽度”保持在 10% 以下。一旦“宽度”超过 40%，重复音的音高变化可能会产生不悦耳的刺耳噪音，尤其是在与高频率结合使用时。最后，“空间” 参数允许你控制效果的立体声宽度。

    The parameters delay (depending on plugin the initial or average delay time) and the width (a measure of the size of the delay time variations) give you additional control over the oscillations. Again we can go by the same rule of thumb: higher values result in a stronger chorus effect. To leave the effect in the background, keep the width below 10 %. Once the width goes past 40 %, the pitch variations of the duplicate can produce unpleasing dissonances, especially when combined with a high rate. Last but not least, the spatial parameter allows you to control the stereo width of the effect.









    • 何时使用合唱

    • When To Use Chorus





    歌曲的背景音轨（弦乐、合成器音垫、和声以及节奏吉他，但后者相对较少）非常适合使用合唱效果。通过合适的设置，合唱效果可以将相对稀疏的背景音变成厚实而柔和的层次感。

    The tracks that make up the background layer of a song (strings, pads, background vocals and to a lesser extend rhythm guitars) are the perfect candidates for chorusing. With the right settings, the chorus effect will turn a relatively sparse background into a thick and soft layer.





    至于主唱部分，加入一些合唱效果或许能为略显单薄的嗓音增添一些深度，但务必尽可能使用得当，以保持人声的自然音色不受影响。一个有趣的变通方法是只在某些乐句（例如副歌的结尾）中使用合唱效果，营造出其他歌手在歌曲关键歌词处加入合唱的错觉。

    As for the lead vocals, a little chorus might add some depth to a thin voice, but the effect should be applied as subtle as possible so that the natural sound of the voice remains intact. An interesting variation is to apply the chorus effect only to certain phrases (for example the end of the refrain), giving the impression that other singers join in at lyric lines that are central to the song.





    如果你的贝斯线条节奏不快，而是着重于构建稳定的基础，那么你可以尝试用低速率合唱效果器为其添加一些悦耳的振荡效果。这是一种让略显静态的贝斯线条“鲜活起来”的好方法。我们还可以继续探讨下去，但我还是把实验留给你自己去探索，这样会更有启发意义。

    If you've got a bass line that is not moving too quickly and instead focuses on laying a stable foundation, you might want to add a nice oscillating effect to it using a low rate chorus. It is a nice way of making a somewhat static bass "come to life". We could go on and on, but it is much more instructive if I leave the experimenting up to you.





    -------------------------------------

    -------------------------------------





    简而言之 - 合唱

    In A Nutshell - Chorus





    • 合唱效果模拟了合唱团的声音，给人一种多种乐器同时演奏而不是只有一种乐器演奏的错觉。



    • The chorus effect simulates a choir. It gives the impression that multiple instruments are playing instead of just one.



    • 它是通过复制一份文件，然后将复制的文件延迟不同时长播放而产生的。这也会产生不同程度的音调变化。



    • It is produced by creating a duplicate and delaying the duplicate by a varying amount. This also creates a varying pitch shift.



    • 除非你是在制作迷幻音乐，否则请以微妙的方式使用它。



    • Apply it in a subtle manner unless you are producing psychedelic music.



    • 非常适合合唱的是构成背景的音轨：背景人声、弦乐、合成器音垫和节奏吉他。

    • Perfect for chorusing are the tracks that make up the background: background vocals, strings, pads and rhythm guitars.





    -------------------------------------

    -------------------------------------









    1.7 其他影响

    1.7. Other Effects





    很遗憾，我们无法一一介绍所有优秀的音频效果。但还有一些值得一提的，它们或许能在您优化混音时派上用场。

    Unfortunately, it is not possible to have a look at all the fantastic audio effects that are out there. But there are a few more that deserve being mentioned and that might come in handy as you are working on optimizing your mix.









    • 兴奋剂

    • Exciters





    激励器（也称增强器）总是笼罩着一层神秘的面纱。它们是相对较新的设备，最早于上世纪七十年代问世，在数字时代到来之前，对于家庭录音音乐人甚至小型录音棚来说，价格都过于昂贵。如今，高质量的激励器插件售价低至 250 美元（例如 Aphex Vintage Aural Exciter），甚至还有一些免费软件也能提供令人满意的效果（例如 Elogoxa 的 X-Cita）。

    Exciters (also called enhancers) have an aura of mystery surrounding them. They are relatively new devices, first used in the seventies, and have been too expensive for home-recoding musicians and even small studios until the dawn of the digital age. Today high quality exciter plugins are available for as little as $ 250 (Aphex Vintage Aural Exciter) and there are even some freeware exciters out there that produce acceptable results (X-Cita by Elogoxa).













    （X-cita 插件）

    (X-cita Plugin)





    当你给声音添加失真效果时，会产生大量的高频谐波。这本身就是一个自然现象。然而，这些新增的谐波是随机的，与音乐中的基音无关。因此，整体效果往往显得不和谐。激励器的作用在于确保只保留与音乐相关的谐波，从而赋予声音一种独特而饱满的光泽。

    When you add distortion to sound, a large number of high-frequency harmonics appear. This is just a natural process. However, these added harmonics are random and do not relate to the fundamental notes in your music. So the overall effect is rather dissonant. Exciters make sure that only the harmonics relevant to the music are kept, giving the sound an interesting and thick sparkle.





    不妨试试——你的音乐或许能从这些额外的和声中受益，尤其是在混音中有很多（相对缺乏生气的）MIDI音轨的情况下。一如既往，要保持微妙，并尽可能将其应用于单个乐器，而不是立体声输出。过多的“刺激”很快就会变得刺耳、不自然，而且令人疲惫。

    Try it out - your music might profit from this additional harmonic content, especially if there are a lot of (relatively lifeless) MIDI tracks in the mix. As always, keep it subtle and use it on individual instruments rather than the stereo output if possible. Too much "excitement" can quickly become harsh, unnatural and fatiguing.









    • 饱和

    • Saturation





    在 80 年代，制作干净、精致的混音需要专业的录音棚、昂贵的尖端设备和顶尖的音乐家。随着数字音频工作站（DAW）和虚拟插件（VST）的兴起，制作干净的音频变得便宜得多。这算是好事吗？这取决于你问谁。许多制作人和音乐爱好者认为，如今的音乐太干净、太冷漠。他们怀念模拟音频设备赋予歌曲的那种“脏”的温暖感。

    In the 80s it took professional studios with expensive state-of-the-art equipment and top musicians to produce a clean and polished mix. With the rise of DAWs and VST instruments, producing clean audio has become a lot cheaper. Is this a happy end? Depends on who you ask. Many producers and music enthusiasts claim that today's music is too clean and too cold. They miss the "dirty" warmth analog audio devices forced onto a song.





    如果您也有同感，那么您会很高兴地听到，借助饱和度插件，您可以重现经典的模拟音色。它们通过在混音中添加柔和的失真和非线性压缩来实现这一目标，这两种效果在电子管或磁带设备的音频播放中都非常典型。许多音频工程师在母带处理阶段使用饱和度插件，以一种微妙的方式将其应用于整个混音，使各个部分更加融合。

    If you feel the same way, you will be happy to hear that with the help of saturation plugins you can revive the good ol' analog sound. They accomplish this task by adding soft distortion and non-linear compression to the mix, both effects that are very typical for audio playback on tube or tape devices. Many audio engineers use saturation in the mastering phase, applying the effect in a subtle fashion across the entire mix to glue it together.





    用于母带处理的热门饱和度插件是 PSP 出品的 Vintage Warmer（售价 150 美元）。如果您只是想尝试一下这种效果，或者预算有限，也可以选择一些免费软件，例如音频博主 Variety Of Sound 开发的 FerrisTDS。FerrisTDS 的预设功能可以让您快速上手，找到适合您音乐的饱和度效果。

    A popular saturation plugin for mastering purposes is Vintage Warmer by PSP ($ 150). For those who just want to try out the effect or are on a tight budget, there are freeware alternatives such as FerrisTDS by the audio blogger Variety Of Sound. The presets allow you to jump right in and see what fits your music.













    （FerrisTDS 插件）

    (FerrisTDS Plugin)









    1.8 自动化

    1.8. Automation

    进步意味着改变；完美意味着经常改变——温斯顿·丘吉尔

    To improve is to change; to be perfect is to change often - Winston Churchill









    自动化是提升混音效果的另一个强大工具。它可以使音轨更加流畅，赋予原本冰冷机械的 MIDI 乐器以生命力，优化歌曲的动态范围，并创造巧妙的特效。它的可能性无穷无尽。所以，如果你之前没有使用过自动化，一定要把它加入你的工具箱。

    Another great tool for getting the most out of your mix is automation. It can smoothen a track, bring life to a cold and machine-like MIDI instrument, optimize the dynamics of a song and create neat special effects. The possibilities are endless. So if you haven't used automation before, make sure to include it in your toolbox in the future.









    • 原则

    • The Principle





    当你设定好音轨的音量后，它会在整首歌中保持不变。音轨的声像位置、均衡器衰减的增益、混响的混音电平、激励器的旁通设置等等也是如此。一旦设定好，它们就会在整个混音过程中保持不变。但这并非必须如此。

    When you choose the volume of a track, it remains at this level throughout the entire song. Same goes for the pan position of the track, the gain of your EQ cut, the mix level of the reverb, the bypass setting of the exciter, and so on. Once chosen, it will remain unchanged for the duration of the mix. But this does not need to be.





    几乎所有 DAW 都允许将任何参数用作变量。你可以通过自动化音量来实现乐器平滑的淡入效果，通过自动化声像位置让乐器在立体声场中自由移动，通过自动化均衡器的增益参数使 EQ 衰减在歌曲开头更加明显，等等。几乎任何参数都可以随时间变化，唯一的限制就是你的时间和想象力。

    Almost all DAWs offer the possibility to use any parameter as a variable. You can achieve a smooth instrument fade-in by automating its volume level, have the instrument wander across the stereo field by automating the pan position, make an EQ cut more pronounced as the hook begins by automating the EQ's gain parameter, and so on. You can make almost any parameter time-dependent, the only limit is your time and imagination.





    在 Cubase 中使用自动化非常简单，只需激活音轨的写入按钮，然后在播放歌曲的同时进行所需的更改即可。您所做的更改将保存到单独的自动化音轨中（每个音轨对应播放期间更改的一个参数）。您可以随时返回到这些自动化音轨进行编辑。要打开音频轨道的自动化音轨，请右键单击该音频轨道并选择“显示已使用的自动化”。

    In Cubase using automation is as simple as activating the write button of a track and doing all the desired changes while playing back the song. The changes you make will be saved in separate automation tracks (one track for each parameter that was altered during the playback). You can always come back to the automation tracks at a later point to edit them. To open the automation tracks of an audio track, right click on the audio track and select "Show Used Automation".





    有时我会启用写入功能，随意更改某个参数，只是为了创建相应的自动化轨道。然后我会手动输入所需的自动化参数，这通常比在播放过程中记录更改更精确。请务必在输入更改后播放歌曲时启用读取按钮。否则，自动化参数将无法读取。

    Sometimes I activate the write function and do a random change on a parameter just to create the corresponding automation track. Then I put in the desired automation manually, which is usually more precise than recording the changes during playback. Make sure to activate the read button when playing the song after you put in the changes. Otherwise the automation will not be read.













    （音轨的读写按钮）

    (A Track's Read And Write Buttons)













    （自动音轨导入，自动音量级别示例）

    (Opening Automation Track, Example Of Automated Volume Level)









    • 一些灵感

    • Some Inspiration





    正如前文所述，可能性无穷无尽。因此，我们在此仅列举一些灵感来源。有些技巧较为微妙，可用于柔化或拓宽混音；另一些则非常显著，可在适当情况下用作特殊效果。

    As mentioned, the possibilities are endless. So we limit ourselves here to listing a few ideas for inspiration. Some are subtle and serve to smoothen or widen a mix, others are very much noticeable and can be used as special effects when appropriate.





    体积：

    Volume:





    • 对各个音轨进行淡入淡出处理，可以使声音更加流畅。这也有助于将音轨更好地融入混音中。



    • Fade-ins and fade-outs of individual tracks for a more smooth sound. Also helps in embedding the tracks in the mix.



    • 交叉淡入淡出，即让一个音轨淡出，另一个音轨淡入。这种处理方式常用于歌曲中同时出现的两句歌词，或以更自然的方式合并不同的录音版本。



    • Cross-fade two tracks, that is, have the one fade-out while the other fades in. Often used to overlap two simultaneous lyric lines in a song or merge different recording takes in a more natural fashion.



    • 把独奏的开头音量调大，以吸引听众的注意力。



    • Make the beginning of a solo louder to grab the listener's attention.



    • 强调歌曲的特定部分，例如副歌、过渡段或间奏。

    • Emphasize specific parts of a song such as the chorus, bridge or interlude.





    平移：

    Panning:





    • 副歌部分将背景音乐的声像拉宽。



    • Pan background tracks wider in the chorus.



    • 让音轨在立体声场中移动（如果你想听听这个例子，可以听听 Meat Loaf 的《I'd Do Anything For Love》开头的吉他声）。



    • Have a track move across the stereo field (if you'd like to hear an example of this, check out the guitar at the beginning Meat Loaf's "I'd Do Anything For Love").



    • 让一段音乐在淡出时移到一边，以突出音量自动化效果。

    • Have a track move to the side as it fades out to underline the volume automation.





    情商：

    EQ:





    • 在只有少数乐器演奏的部分（例如：前奏）增强中低频，以获得温暖饱满的声音。



    • Boost the lower midrange during parts in which only a few instruments are active (for example: intro) for a warm and full sound.



    • 在歌曲的过渡部分，让主唱的声音听起来像是通过电话传来的。这样可以吸引听众的注意力，并为歌曲增添变化。为了达到电话音效，需要衰减 800 Hz 以下和 3000 Hz 以上的频率，并提升中间的所有频率，直到出现失真。提升幅度应在 1500 Hz 左右达到最大值。

    • Have the lead vocals sound like they are coming through a telephone during the bridge. Grabs the listener's attention and gives variety to the sound. To achieve a telephone sound, cut everything below 800 Hz and above 3.000 Hz and boost everything in between until distortions appear. The boost should be at maximum level at around 1.500 Hz.





    效果：

    Effects:





    • 利用混响、延迟、失真等效果来强调歌词中的个别词语，以突出它们对歌词信息的重要性。



    • Emphasize individual words in the lyrics with reverb, delay, distortion, etc ... to underline their importance to the message.



    • 在副歌部分调高效果器的混音参数，使其更加突出。

    • Turn up the mix parameter of your effects during the chorus to have it really stand out.













    2. 混合

    2. Mixing









    2.1 全局概览

    2.1. The Big Picture

    整体大于部分之和——亚里士多德

    The whole is more than the sum of its parts - Aristotle









    到目前为止，我们一直在学习音乐制作中常用的效果器以及如何自动化音轨。现在我们已经熟悉了这些，是时候进入正题了。你已经创作了歌曲，录制了所有音轨（或者创建了 MIDI 文件，或者两者都做了），并将所有需要导入的素材导入了 DAW（数字音频工作站）。混音阶段由此开始。混音的最终目标是将各个音轨融合成一个统一的、三维立体的混音。

    Up to now, all we've been doing is learning about the effects that are commonly applied in music production and how to automate tracks. Now that we are familiar with that, it's time to get to business. You've written the song, recorded all the tracks (or created the MIDI file or both) and imported whatever needs to be imported into the DAW. This is where the mixing phase begins. The ultimate goal of mixing is to turn the separate tracks into a homogeneous, three-dimensional mix.





    好的混音应该具备哪些要素？问十位音频工程师，你可能会得到二十个答案。每位音乐人和音频工程师对好的混音都有自己的理解。因此，我们将以下列表限定为一些共同点——大多数音乐人和音频工程师都会认为好的混音应该具备的特征。

    What constitutes a good mix? Ask ten audio engineers and you'll get twenty answers. Each musician and audio engineer has his or her own idea about what a good mix should sound like. That's why we'll restrict the following list to common denominators - elements that most musicians and audio engineers would name as characteristics of a good mix.





    • 清晰度：尽管混音的目标是均衡统一，但每种乐器都应该清晰可辨。你肯定不希望贝斯和底鼓混成一团轰鸣的“东西”。好的混音应该让你的耳朵能够分辨出贝斯和底鼓是两个独立的部分。



    • Clarity: Despite aiming for a homogeneous mix, each instrument should be clearly heard. You don't want the bass and kick merging into a boomy "something". In a good mix, your ears will be able to locate the bass and kick as separate parts.



    • 多维性：能够在混音中定位乐器意味着感知到它处于一个独立的空间。好的混音应该给人一种错觉，仿佛有些乐器在左边，有些在右边，有些在前面，有些在后面。



    • Multi-Dimensionality: Being able to locate an instrument in the mix means perceiving it as being in its own space. A good mix should give the illusion that some instruments are to the left, some to the right, some in the front and some in the back.



    • 平衡：好的混音应该兼顾左右平衡和频谱平衡。频谱平衡指的是不同频段（例如低音、中低频、中高频、空气感）的比例应该自然和谐。你肯定不希望低音盖过其他所有声音。



    • Balance: A good mix should have left-right balance as well as spectral balance. The latter means that the different frequency bands (such as bass, lower mids, upper mids, air) should be in a natural or pleasing proportion. You don't want the bass overpowering everything else.



    • 重点：一首歌的副歌部分应该朗朗上口，无需使用花哨的混音和母带处理技巧就能听起来悦耳动听。这是词曲作者的职责。但在优秀的混音中，副歌部分会通过各种恰当的方式加以强调——例如效果、自动化处理和动态变化。



    • Emphasis: The hook of a song should be catchy and sound well without the use of hoity toity mixing and mastering tricks. This is the songwriter's job. But in a good mix, the hook is emphasized by all means appropriate - effects, automation, dynamic variation.



    • 最终定稿：是的，接下来会进行母带处理。但母带处理的目的只是对已经完成的混音进行润色，解决所有问题。母带处理并不能把平庸的混音变成优秀的混音。混音本身就应该已经非常出色了。



    • Finalized: Yes, the mastering phase will follow. But it is only meant to polish a completed mix in which all problems are taken care of. Mastering does not turn a flat mix into a great one. The mix should already sound spectacular on its own.



    • 动态余量：在母带处理阶段，可能需要进行一些均衡调整或细微效果处理。好的混音峰值不会超过 -4 dB，从而为最终润色留出足够的动态空间。不必担心响度优化，这是母带处理阶段的一部分。

    • Headroom: During the mastering phase it might be necessary to apply some EQ changes or subtle effects. A good mix doesn't peak above - 4 dB, thus leaving enough dynamic space for the final polishing. Don't worry about optimizing loudness, this is part of the mastering stage.





    务必理解并记住这些要素。运用你所学的关于效果器和自动化的知识，以及本章将要介绍的混音策略，尽力在你的混音中“实现”它们。

    Make sure to understand and remember each of these elements. Try your best to "make them happen" in your mix by applying what you've learned about effects and automation as well as the mixing strategy that will be laid out in this chapter.









    2.2 混合策略

    2.2. Mixing Strategy

    细节决定成败——桑福德·威尔

    Details create the big picture - Sanford I. Weill









    • 混合空间

    • The Mixing Space





    混音是一个非常个性化的过程，没有一套固定的混音流程可以保证最终获得最佳混音效果。适用于一种音乐类型的方法，可能并不适用于另一种。因此，保持开放的心态，并根据你的音乐风格、音乐理念和个人视角，选择最能带来满意效果的方法至关重要。相应地，以下混音策略仅供参考，而非一成不变的准则。

    Mixing is a very individual process, there's no default mixing chain we can go through to arrive at the best mix possible. What works for one genre, might fail in another. So it's important to keep an open mind and adopt what produces the most pleasing results for your genre, your style and your perspective on music. Accordingly, the following mixing strategy should be taken as a suggestion rather than a set of axioms written in stone.





    为了理解这种混音策略背后的理念，不妨在脑海中想象一个三维坐标系。它有两个轴，分别代表平面和高度。其中一个平面轴代表左右方向，另一个代表深度。高度轴则代表频率范围。我们的任务是为混音中的每个音轨在混音空间中分配一个相对独立的区域。

    To understand the idea behind this mixing strategy, picture a three-dimensional coordinate system in your mind. It has two axis that spawn the flat ground and one height axis. One of the two ground axis symbolizes the left-right direction, while the other represents depth. The height axis stands for the frequency range. Our job is to assign each track in our mix a more or less isolated region in the mixing space.













    （三维混合空间）

    (Three-Dimensional Mixing Space)





    例如，考虑一个被置于右侧 40% 声像定位的节奏吉他，它位于混音的背景中，频率范围为 80 - 5000 Hz。这三个信息确定了节奏吉他在混音空间中的位置。当添加另一个音轨时，我们希望尽量减少重叠。例如，一个被置于中间声像定位、位于混音的前方、频率范围同样为 40 - 5000 Hz 的贝斯可能会与节奏吉他产生冲突。虽然在左右和深度方向上的分离度足够，但频率重叠可能会迫使我们通过均衡器进行衰减来做出妥协。

    Consider for example a rhythm guitar that is panned 40 % to the right, is in the background of the mix and ranges from 80 - 5.000 Hz. These three pieces of information locate the rhythm guitar in our mixing space. When adding another track to it, we want to minimize overlapping. For example, a bass that is panned to the center, is in the front of the mix and ranges from 40 - 5.000 Hz might come in conflict with the rhythm guitar. While sufficiently separated in left-right and depth direction, the frequency overlap might force us to make sacrifices by applying EQ cuts.





    另一方面，如果我们再加入一把频率范围在 80-5000 Hz 的吉他，由于重叠区域过大，均衡器衰减就无法解决问题了（不过，互补衰减或许仍然是个好办法）。这时我们需要采用其他分离方法：例如，将其向左声道偏移 40%，或者将其置于混音的中间位置。无论我们最终采取什么方法，都应该服务于一个最终目标：最大限度地减少左右声道、深度和频率上的重叠。

    On the other hand, if we add another guitar that also ranges from 80 - 5.000 Hz, EQ cuts won't do the trick anymore since the overlapping region is so large (complementary cuts might still be a good idea though). Here we have to take other means of separation: pan it 40 % to the left for example and/or put it in the middle of the mix. Whatever we decide to do, it should serve the ultimate goal: minimize left-right, depth and frequency overlapping.





    这种混音方法乍看之下可能过于抽象，但它却是同时实现清晰度、多维性和左右平衡的绝佳途径。当然，你无需记住所有频率范围才能做到这一点。为了尽量减少频率重叠，你只需知道某些乐器组合（例如贝斯和底鼓、贝斯和吉他、吉他和镲片）可能需要你进行一些频率削减即可。

    This approach to mixing might seem unnecessarily abstract at first, but it is a great way to achieve clarity, multi-dimensionality and left-right balance at the same time. Of course you don't have memorize all the frequency ranges for this to work. To minimize frequency overlaps it is sufficient to know that the combination of certain instruments (bass and kick, bass and guitar, guitar and cymbals) might force you to make some cuts.









    • 步步

    • Step By Step





    在开始分离各个音轨之前，你应该先在每条音轨上添加最重要的效果。如果之后再添加，可能会迫使你重新考虑乐器在混音中的位置，最终可能需要重新调整所有音轨。例如，如果你想在节奏吉他上添加合唱效果，那就从一开始就添加。音轨的音量也是如此。尽早设置好音量，才能把握整体效果。

    You should include the most important effects on the individual tracks before you start separating them. Including them at a later point might force you to rethink the instrument's place in the mix and then you might end up reorganizing all the tracks. So if you want a chorus on the rhythm guitar, insert the effect at the very beginning. Same goes for the volume level of the tracks. Set them early on to have the "big picture".





    大致设置好音量、插入效果器并将所有音轨分配到混音空间中的相应区域后，就可以进行频谱平衡和自动化处理（例如，突出副歌部分并使过渡更加平滑）。频谱平衡可以像调整几个音量推子一样简单，也可以像使用多频段压缩器一样复杂——选择合适的方法即可。最后，如有必要，进行一些故障排除。这样就完成了混音。

    Once you roughly set the volume levels, inserted the effects and assigned all the tracks their proper region in the mixing space, you can move on to spectral balancing and automation (for example to emphasize the hook and smoothen transitions). Balancing the spectral bands can be as easy as adjusting some volume faders or as complex as using a multi-band compressor - whatever seems appropriate. Last but not least, do some troubleshooting if necessary. This should finalize the mix.





    以下是混合策略的概要：

    Here's the summary of the mixing strategy:





    1. 导入参考音轨

    1. Import Reference Track

    2. 大致设定音量水平

    2. Roughly Set Volume Levels

    3. 在音轨上插入效果

    3. Insert Effects On Tracks

    4. 按频率、深度和左右方向分离音轨

    4. Separate Tracks By Frequency, Depth and Left-Right

    5. 频谱平衡

    5. Spectral Balancing

    6. 自动化

    6. Automation

    7. 故障排除

    7. Troubleshooting





    故障排除不必等到最后。如果发现问题，应尽快处理，以免拖延，甚至（更糟糕的是）在混音过程中暴露出来。最终的故障排除是为了确保任何问题都不会影响到母带处理阶段。

    Troubleshooting does not have to be postponed till the end. If you notice a problem, take care of it as soon as you can as not to drag it along or (even worse) end up pronouncing it during the mixing process. The final troubleshoot is there to guarantee that no problems spill over into the mastering phase.





    你可能已经注意到，我们还有一个要点还没提到：参考曲目。混音时，很容易陷入细节，或者忽略过重的低音。因此，时不时地切换到一首已经混音和母带处理完毕的歌曲非常重要。这能帮助你注意到一些在混音过程中可能已经习以为常的问题。那么，应该选择哪首歌作为参考呢？它可以是你所在音乐类型中具有你想要达到的音色的热门歌曲，也可以是你之前混音效果非常好的作品。

    You might have noticed that there's one point we haven't talked about yet: the reference track. When mixing, it is easy to get lost in details or lose sight of an overpowering bass. That's why it's important to switch to a fully mixed and mastered song from time to time. It will help you to notice problems you might have already gotten used to while working on your mix. Which song to choose as reference? It could be a hit song from your genre that has the sound you'd like to achieve or one of your earlier mixes that turned out really well.









    • 结语

    • Final Remarks





    永远不要忘记休息。参考曲目虽然能有效避免思维定势（或者更确切地说是听觉定势），但并不能让你完全免疫。千万不要试图一口气完成混音。先做一个粗略的混音，然后休息一下，或者至少喝杯咖啡，看一集《辛普森一家》。如果混音中还有什么不对劲的地方，休息一段时间后再回来，你会立刻听出来。

    Never forget to take breaks. While the reference track helps a lot in avoiding tunnel vision (or rather tunnel hearing), it does not make you immune to it. Never try to finish a mix in one continuous session. Get a rough mix ready, then sleep on it or at least have a coffee break and watch an episode of "The Simpsons". If there's still something off in the mix, you'll immediately hear it when you get back to the mix after a long break.





    在休息之前，不妨花几分钟时间制作几个备选版本。如果您觉得歌曲适合柔和的人声，可以导出“柔和人声”混音版本。如果您对更具冲击力的吉他音色感兴趣，可以保存“强劲吉他”混音版本。现在正是尝试的好时机，当您继续混音时，这些备选版本将对您大有帮助，引导您找到正确的方向。

    Before you take a break, you might want to spend a few minutes creating alternate versions. If you think the song could profit from softer vocals, export a "vocals soft" mix. If the idea of a more aggressive guitar intrigues you, save a "guitar sharp" mix. This is the time to experiment and when you resume the mixing session, these alternative versions will be very helpful in guiding you into the right direction.





    如果你混音的歌曲并非由你创作或演奏，最好不要让词曲作者或乐队成员过多地参与混音过程。首先，他们可能不愿意为了获得清晰的混音效果而做出必要的妥协。其次，每个乐队成员都可能坚持突出自己的乐器，而忽略了整体效果。

    If you mix a song that was not written or performed by you, it is a good idea not to involve the songwriters or the performing band too closely in the mixing process. For one, it is likely that they are not willing to make the sacrifices necessary to create a clear mix. Also, each band member might insist on having his or her instrument emphasized without taking into account the big picture.





    因此，与其团队合作混音，不如先采访词曲作者或乐队成员，了解他们对歌曲的构想，然后独自制作一个粗混版本。粗混完成后，征求他们的修改意见，并根据这些意见最终确定混音版本（或者再制作一个粗混版本）。这种方法很好地兼顾了艺术家的构想和他们对于如何实现这一构想的主观看法。

    So instead of mixing as a team, interview the songwriters or band members to understand their vision of the song and make a rough mix by yourself. After the rough mix is complete, ask for revision requests and finalize the mix (or make another rough mix) according to those. This approach is a good compromise between the vision of the artists and their very subjective perspective on how to achieve it during mixing.









    2.3. 分离轨道

    2.3. Separating Tracks

    平等与隔离无法共存——杰森·玛耶兹

    Equality and separation cannot exist in the same space - Jason Mraz









    粗略地设置音量并添加效果器，这是我们混音策略的前两个步骤，此处无需赘述，因为第一章已经介绍了使用效果器的基本技巧。不过，我们将详细阐述一下如何分离音轨。

    Roughly setting the volume levels and inserting the effects, the first two steps in our mixing strategy, need no further explanation at this point as the basic tips on using effects were included in chapter one. However, we will elaborate a bit on separating the tracks.





    我们的目标是按频率、深度和左右方向分离音轨。按这个顺序吗？是的，就是按这个顺序。按左右方向分离就像旋转声像旋钮一样简单。如果你从这个（最显而易见的）步骤开始，频率重叠和深度造成的冲突就会变得不那么明显，尤其对于未经训练的耳朵来说。所以，先从不太明显的步骤开始，尝试在旋转声像旋钮之前获得令人满意的分离效果。这将有助于你最大限度地利用混音空间。

    Our goal is to separate the tracks by frequency, depth and left-right. In this order? Yes, in this order. Separating by left-right is as simple as turning the pan knob. If you start with this (most obvious) step, conflicts due to frequency overlapping and depth will become less noticeable, especially to the untrained ear. So start with the least obvious steps and try to achieve a pleasing separation before you begin to turn the pan knob. This will help you to get the most out of the space available to your mix.









    • 频率

    • Frequency





    你的混音中包含很多音轨，但只有一个可听频段（16-20,000 Hz），因此要谨慎管理，并做好取舍的准备，避免最终得到浑浊不清的声音。 第 1.3 章的“快速提示” 部分已经提到了最常见的冲突以及避免方法。

    You've got a lot of tracks in your mix but only one audible frequency band (spanning from 16 - 20.000 Hz), so manage wisely and be willing to make sacrifices to prevent ending up with a muddy mess. The most common conflicts as well as ways to prevent them have been mentioned in the Quick Tips section in chapter 1.3.













    （辅助调整：左声道底鼓均衡，右声道贝斯均衡）

    (Complementary Cuts: Left Kick EQ, Right Bass EQ)









    • 深度

    • Depth





    为了了解如何在混音中营造深度感，我们来看看声波在空气中传播时的变化。理想情况下，波阵面会在声源周围形成一个球形。随着声波的传播，这个球形会不断扩大。这意味着波阵面中包含的初始能量会分散到一个不断增大的表面积上，因此，声波的响度会降低。所以，远处的声源音量较低也就不足为奇了。这一点显而易见，以至于很多人往往忽略了音量也是强调深度感的重要因素。举个例子：如果距离增加一倍，音量就会下降 6 分贝。

    To find out how a sense of depth can be introduced in a mix, let's take a look at how sound waves change as they travel through air. Ideally, a wave front forms a sphere around the sound source. As the sound waves propagate, this sphere grows. This means that the initial energy contained in the wave front is spread over an ever-increasing surface area and accordingly, the loudness of the sound waves decreases. So, no surprise here, distance sources are at a lower volume level. This is so obvious that many tend to forget that volume is a great way to underline depth. Just for reference: if the distance doubles, the volume goes down by 6 dB.





    另一个显而易见的现象是，远处声源的声音到达我们耳中的时间会稍晚一些。由于声音在室温下的传播速度约为每秒 330 米，这意味着每增加一米的距离，声音到达我们耳中的时间就会比近处声源延迟3 毫秒（并非回声）。因此，如果鼓手位于吉他手身后五米处，鼓声到达我们耳中的时间就会晚 15 毫秒。您可以使用音频事件的信息栏进行精确的调整。此方法适用于音频和 MIDI 音轨。对于 MIDI 音轨，您还可以使用“MIDI 修饰符”效果来调整音轨位置。顺便一提：此效果还可以通过引入位置、音高、力度和长度的随机变化，使 MIDI 乐器听起来更加逼真。

    Another obvious effect is that the sound of distant sources reaches us a little later. Since sound travels at around 330 meters per second at room temperature, this means that for every meter distance there's a delay (not in the sense of echo) of 3 milliseconds compared to sources that are right next to us. So if the drummer is located five meters behind the guitarist, the drum sound will reach us 15 milliseconds later. Use the info bar of an audio event for precise shifting. This works for both audio and MIDI tracks. For MIDI tracks you can also the "MIDI Modifiers" effect to shift the track. Just by the way: this effect is also very helpful in making MIDI instruments sound more realistic by introducing random variations in position, pitch, velocity and length.













    （Cubase 信息栏中高亮显示事件开始位置）

    (Info Bar In Cubase With Event Start Location Highlighted)













    （Cubase 中的“MIDI 修饰符”效果）

    ("MIDI Modifiers" Effect In Cubase)





    此外，空气对不同频率的吸收也不均匀。如前所述，空气对高频的衰减比低频更强。因此，空气在传播声波时就像一个低通滤波器。距离声源越远，高通滤波的效果就应该越强。

    Then there's the uneven absorption of frequencies by air. As already mentioned, air dampens higher frequencies more strongly than lower frequencies. So air acts like a low-pass filer as it transmits sound waves. The greater the distance to a source, the stronger the high-cut should be.





    来自远距离声源的声音通常包含较少的直达声和较多的反射声。你可以在数字音频工作站（DAW）中通过提高混响插件的混合和扩散参数来模拟这种效果。当然，增强延迟（即回声效果）也能达到同样的效果。其他插件也能帮助增加声音的深度，例如合唱效果器和其他调制效果器，这些效果器通常都会使音轨更加突出。

    Sound coming from a source at great distance generally contains less direct sound and more reflected sound. You can simulate this in a DAW by turning up the mix and diffusion parameter in the reverb plugin. Of course making the delay (in the sense of echo) more noticeable works just as well. Other plugins can also help in creating more depth, among them chorus as well as other modulation effects, which all tend to push a track in the background.





    以下是为歌曲增加深度的一些方法概述：

    Here's a summary of how to add depth to a track:





    1. 降低音量

    1. Lower The Volume

    2. 稍微调整信号的起始点

    2. Shift The Signal's Starting Point Slightly

    3. 剪个高发型

    3. Apply A High-Cut

    4. 增加混响中的混合和扩散

    4. Increase Mix And Diffusion In Reverb

    5. 添加合唱

    5. Add Chorus









    • 从左到右

    • Left-Right





    一旦频率冲突得到解决，乐器也“配备”了一些深度，就可以调整声像旋钮了。这无疑是让各个音轨之间产生距离感的最明显方法。但是，每个乐器应该放在哪个声像位置呢？这主要取决于你和你的歌曲，但有一些值得注意的事项。

    Once frequency conflicts are taken care of and the instruments are "equipped" with some depth, it's time to turn the pan knob. This will no doubt be the most noticeable way of getting some distance between the individual tracks. But where to pan which instrument? This is mostly up to you and your song, but there are some things worth keeping in mind.





    始终将贝斯、底鼓、大提琴和暗色调合成器音色等低频乐器保持在靠近中央的位置。这样做有两个重要原因。首先，低频段包含了混音中的大部分能量，因此将其均匀分配到两个扬声器上是合理的。这也有助于后续实现左右声道平衡。其次，低音较重的声源通常更难定位，即使它们不在中央，也会被感知为来自中央。因此，除非有充分的理由，否则不要将低音乐器的声像移动超过 15%。还有一点需要注意：既然我们决定将底鼓放在中央，那么将其他鼓组音轨大幅度地移动声像就意义不大（除非出于艺术目的）。为了获得自然的声音，我们需要将它们保持在底鼓附近。

    Always keep low frequency instruments such as the bass, kick, cello and dark pads close to the center. There are two good reasons for this. Firstly, the bass band contains most of the energy in a mix and it thus makes sense to distribute the load evenly between the two speakers. This also makes it easier to achieve left-right balance later on. Secondly, bass-heavy sound sources are generally more difficult to locate and are perceived as coming from the center even if they aren't there. So only pan bass instruments by more than 15 % if there's a really good reason to do so. One more thing to keep in mind: since we've decided to leave the kick in the center, it wouldn't make much sense to pan other drum tracks widely (unless for artistic reasons). For a natural sound we need to keep them in the vicinity of the kick.





    另一个通常位于正中央的音轨是主唱。毕竟，它是歌曲的核心元素，这种声像定位方式恰恰突显了它的重要性。至于和声，传统上会将其声像定位得非常宽，以覆盖整个混音。如果你有多条和声，可以将其分布在左右声道，这种方法效果很好。但如果只有一条和声呢？在这种情况下，明智的做法是减少声像定位，并找到一种方法，用其他伴奏乐器来平衡和声。或者，你可以将和声轨道复制一份，然后用副本进行平衡。

    Another track that is usually kept right in the center is the main vocal line. It is, after all, a central element of your song and this way of panning just underlines its importance. As for the background vocals, they are traditionally panned very widely to encompass the entire mix. This works great if you've got multiple background vocals and thus the opportunity to distribute them left and right. But what if there's only one? In this case it's wise to go easier on the panning and find a way to balance the background vocal track with another background instrument. Alternatively, you can double the background vocal track and use the duplicate for balance.





    由于低频乐器、鼓组和主唱位于中间位置，中间部分已经相当拥挤。因此，无论你添加什么其他乐器，都要尽量远离中间位置（例外情况：间奏中代替主唱的独奏吉他）。例如，如果你的混音中包含合成器音垫和节奏吉他，就将其中一个声像定位在左侧 50%，另一个声像定位在右侧 50%。这样，每个音轨都有足够的空间，混音也会更加平衡。

    With the low frequency instruments, drum tracks and main vocals in the center, the center is already quite crowded. So whatever additional instruments you have, keep them away from the center (exception: a solo guitar that takes over for the main vocals during an interlude). For example, if there's a pad and a rhythm guitar in your mix, pan the one 50 % left and the other 50 % right. This way there's enough space for each track and the mix should be fairly balanced.





    避免将乐器声像定位在完全相同的位置。虽然很多乐器都靠近中心，但总可以留出几个百分点的距离。好好利用这一点，哪怕只有几个百分点，也能带来很大的不同。此外，将乐器声像完全移到左侧或右侧通常听起来很不自然。除非这是你整体设计的一部分，否则请避免使用这种极端设置。

    Avoid panning instruments to the exact same spot. Though there are a lot of instruments close to the center, there's always the possibility of getting a few percent between them. Make use of that, a few percent can make a big difference. Also, panning completely left or right often sounds very unnatural. Avoid such extreme settings unless this is part of your grand plan.





    在调整声像时，要注意是否存在不平衡。左右声道输出的电平表应该始终保持在大致相同的高度。这一点适用于歌曲的所有部分，因此请分别检查每个部分。即使您已确保所有音轨组合在一起时（例如在最后的副歌部分）混音平衡，但在只有少数音轨处于活动状态的部分（例如前奏、主歌或间奏）仍然可能存在平衡问题。为避免这种情况，请从歌曲中较为舒缓的部分开始进行声像调整。

    While panning, keep an eye out for imbalances. The meters for the left and right output should always go to about the same height. This is true for all parts of the song, so check them separately. Even when you made sure that the combination of all tracks together (for example during the final chorus) produces a balanced mix, there might still be balance issues during parts with only a few active tracks (such as the intro, verse or interlude). To avoid this, start the panning session with the more laid back parts of the song.





    想要在不进行大幅度声像定位或造成过多频谱损失的情况下，增加乐器之间的距离，立体声增强器是一个不错的选择。它们只需少量调整就能营造出绝佳的立体声效果。不过，大多数立体声增强器也会使低音乐器的位置变宽（而我们希望低音乐器保持居中）。因此，使用时要谨慎，或者更好的选择是使用下一章将要介绍的中侧混音技术来改善立体声效果。虽然这可能需要更多工作，但最终会得到更清晰的混音。

    A nice way to get some more distance between the instruments without resorting to extreme panning or too much loss of spectral content are stereo enhancers. They can produce a spectacular stereo image with very little work. A disadvantage though is that most stereo enhancers also spread the bass instruments (which we want to keep centered). So apply with care or better yet, use the mid-side technique, that is introduced in the next chapter, to improve the stereo image. It might be more work, but will result in a cleaner mix.













    （Cubase中的立体声增强器）

    (Stereo Enhancer in Cubase)





    以下是平移原理的总结：

    Here's a summary of the panning principles:





    1. 中心低频仪器

    1. Low Frequency Instruments In The Center

    2. 主唱和独奏乐器位于中心

    2. Main Vocals And Solo Instruments In The Center

    3. 背景人声的宽广声像定位

    3. Wide Panning Of Background Vocals

    4. 避免镜头反复平移到同一位置

    4. Avoid Panning To The Exact Same Spot

    5. 避免大幅度摇摄

    5. Avoid Extreme Panning

    6. 创造左右平衡

    6. Create Left-Right Balance

    7. 使用立体声增强器或 M/S 以获得更好的立体声效果

    7. Use Stereo Enhancer Or M/S For More Stereo









    3. 掌握

    3. Mastering









    3.1 基本概念

    3.1. Basic Idea

    滚石不生苔，却会变得光滑——奥利弗·赫福德

    A rolling stone gathers no moss, but it gains a certain polish - Oliver Herford









    很多人高估了母带处理对歌曲独特音色的影响。其实，确定音色并解决所有问题是混音阶段的工作。母带处理只是对歌曲进行一些润色，提升音量，并从技术角度进行优化。因此，你应该将大部分精力和时间（90%甚至更多）投入到混音中，尽可能少地留给母带处理。

    Many people overestimate the impact of mastering on a song's characteristic sound. Establishing the sound and fixing all the problems is the job of the mixing phase. Mastering just gives the song a little polish, enhances its loudness and optimizes it from a technical point of view. Accordingly, you should focus most of your energy and time (90 % or more) on mixing and leave as little as possible up to mastering.





    如果混音本身就很糟糕，母带处理也无济于事。它只会让歌曲音量更大、更协调，但不会提升歌曲质量。在这种情况下，重新混音是唯一明智的选择。如果混音本身已经非常出色，那么母带处理阶段应该仅限于优化音量。只有当混音已经很好，但仍然缺乏一些冲击力或存在一些轻微的平衡问题时，才应该考虑使用“完整的母带处理方案”。

    If the mix is bad, mastering will not change this. It will make the song louder and more compatible, but not better. In this case going back to mixing is the only sensible choice. If the mix is fantastic on its own, you can and should limit the mastering phase to optimizing loudness. The "full mastering package" should only be applied to a good mix that is still lacking a bit of punch or has minimal balance issues.





    母带处理通常指的是对立体声进行编辑，因此在这个阶段您将无法单独调整各个音轨。您不能提高某个乐器的音量或改变其声像位置。您所做的任何更改都会应用到整个混音中。为了避免破坏良好的混音效果，所有更改（音量增加除外）都必须非常细微。

    Mastering usually refers to editing the stereo out, so during this phase you won't have access to individual tracks. You cannot make an instrument louder or alter its pan position. Whatever changes you make will be applied across the mix. To not destroy a good mix, all changes (except the loudness increase) must be subtle.





    值得注意的是，如今许多人所说的母带处理（即对歌曲进行最终润色的过程），在音频工程师的早期被称为预母带处理。在数字音频工作站（DAW）时代之前，母带处理指的是制作已完成润色的歌曲的实体拷贝（玻璃母盘），作为后续制作实体拷贝的模板。

    Note that what many nowadays refer to as mastering (the process of giving the song a final polish) was once called pre-mastering by audio engineers. Before the age of digital DAWs, mastering meant creating the physical copy (glass master) of the already polished song that would serve as the model for producing further physical copies.













    （玻璃大师——模拟音乐的圣杯）

    (A Glass Master - The Holy Grail Of Analog Music)









    3.2 掌握战略

    3.2. Mastering Strategy

    策略再精妙，也应该时不时地看看结果——温斯顿·丘吉尔

    However beautiful the strategy, you should occasionally look at the results - Winston Churchill









    假设我们有一个不错的混音，但需要进行一些母带处理。该怎么办呢？和往常一样，没有标准答案。但与混音相比，母带处理方面更容易达成共识。其策略和步骤顺序通常非常相似。因此，您将在下方看到一个相当典型的母带处理流程，但这绝非唯一选择。

    Suppose we have a mix that is good, but in need of a little bit of mastering. What to do? As always, there's no single answer. But in mastering there's much more agreement than in mixing. The strategies and the order in which the steps are taken are often quite similar. So what you find below is a rather typical mastering chain, but by no means the only possibility.





    请记住，母带制作的目的是确保歌曲与各种播放设备的最大兼容性。因此，使用所有可用的设备进行母带制作至关重要。在制作过程中，请分别用扬声器、耳机、车载收音机、电视甚至手机聆听歌曲。记录下各个设备上出现的问题，并尝试在不改变歌曲特性或引入新问题的前提下解决这些问题。务必关闭所有会改变播放效果的功能（例如低音增强、响度调节、立体声调节等）。

    Remember that the mastering process is supposed to guarantee the maximum amount of compatibility with different playback devices. So it is vital that you work with all the equipment available to you. Listen to the song on your loudspeakers, your headphones, your car radio, your television and even the cell phone when mastering. Note the problems that come up on the respective devices and try to get rid of them without changing the song's character or introducing new problems. Make sure to deactivate all functions that alter the playback (bass boost, loudness, stereo).





    另一点需要注意的是“越大越好”的陷阱，我这里指的并非响度大战。出于某些奇怪的心理原因，我们很难判断音量变化带来的整体响度提升或降低。我们往往会认为，声音越大，效果就越好。因此，在使用压缩器时，我总是会调整增益补偿，使整体音量保持不变，以便进行公平的比较。

    Another thing to watch out for is the "louder is better" trap and I'm not referring to the loudness war here. For some odd psychological reasons, we have a hard time judging a change that increases or decreases the overall loudness. We tend to believe that it must be better because it's louder. This is why when applying a compressor, I always choose the make-up gain in a way that will leave the overall volume unchanged to get a fair comparison.





    1. 参考音轨

    1. Reference Track





    第一步应该是将一首制作精良、能够代表你音乐风格的歌曲导入你的 DAW（数字音频工作站）。时不时地进行对比，以确保方向正确。

    Again the first step should be importing a song into your DAW that is well-mastered and representative of your genre. Compare from time to time to stay on track.





    2. 情商

    2. EQ





    在母带处理中，均衡器用于去除低频、消除恼人的共振、建立频谱平衡或仅仅是为了美化混音。为了保持调整的细微性，请务必使用宽范围、低增益的提升或衰减。如果问题仅出现在左声道或右声道，则可以仅在相应的声道上进行必要的均衡调整。只要调整幅度不太大，就不会造成任何平衡问题。

    In mastering the EQ is used to remove the sub-bass, to get rid of awkward resonances, to establish spectral balance or just to sweeten the mix. To keep the changes subtle, make sure to stick to wide, low gain boosts or cuts. If a problem only appears in the left or right channel, feel free to make the necessary EQ incision only in the respective channel. As long as the incision is not too extreme, this shouldn't cause any balance issues.





    3. 峰值限制

    3. Peak-Limiting





    如果你的音乐中存在过多的峰值，可能会在后续处理中造成问题，那么现在就应该使用阈值（输出）合适的限制器来消除它们。为了在不丢失重要内容的情况下消除所有峰值，你可能需要分部分地应用限制器。

    If there are excessive peaks in your music that are likely to cause trouble later on, this is the time to remove them using a limiter with a well-chosen threshold (output). To catch all the peaks without removing relevant content you probably have to apply the limiter part by part.





    此时切记不要过度限制。首先，在母带处理的后续阶段还会使用压缩器和限制器进一步抑制峰值。其次，不要忘记峰值是自然声音不可或缺的一部分。如果无情地去除它们，最终得到的混音会显得异常平淡，缺乏惊喜。

    Make sure not to limit too strongly at this point. For one, a compressor and another limiter will be applied at later stages in the mastering process, further dampening the peaks. Also, don't forget that peaks are an integral part of a natural sound. If you remove them mercilessly, the result will be a strangely flat mix offering few surprises.





    4. 粘合

    4. Glueing





    在这个阶段，你可以添加一些效果，使混音更加均衡。例如，可以添加一个几乎察觉不到的混响，让混音听起来像是在一个共享空间里，或者添加一些饱和度来营造怀旧效果。激励器也可以使用，但必须谨慎操作，因为它们会对声音产生显著影响。

    In this phase you can apply effects to make the mix more homogeneous. This could mean including a hardly noticeable reverb to put the mix in a shared room or some saturation for nostalgic effect. Exciters might work as well, but must be applied carefully since they have a significant impact on the sound.





    5. 压缩

    5. Compressing





    使用压缩器可以使混音更加饱满，并为响度优化做好准备。如果频段平衡良好，且歌曲只需要轻微的压缩，那么单频段压缩器应该是您的首选。但如果仍然存在频谱平衡问题，或者需要更强的压缩效果，则可以考虑使用多频段压缩器。对于本身动态范围就较大的音乐类型（例如管弦乐或原声音乐），不妨尝试使用并行压缩技术。

    Applying the compressor will make the mix more dense and prepare it for loudness optimization. If the frequency bands are well-balanced and the song only requires little compression, a single-band compressor should be your first choice. If on the other hand there are still spectral balance issues or a harder compression is desired, consider using a multi-band compressor instead. For genres that naturally have a large dynamic range (such as orchestral or acoustic music), give the parallel compression technique a try.





    6. 自动化

    6. Automation





    在这个阶段，你还有最后一次机会调整歌曲各部分的音量比例，并添加一些特殊效果，例如在副歌部分添加更宽广的立体声效果。

    This stage offers you one last opportunity to put the parts of the song in the right proportion in terms of volume and add some special effects such as wider stereo in the chorus.





    7. 主限幅

    7. Master-Limiting





    接下来是响度优化。使用限幅器（或最大化器）将音量提升到所需水平。流行或摇滚歌曲母带处理后的典型峰值音量水平为：前奏或间奏 -6 dB，主歌 -3 dB，副歌和独奏接近 0 dB。为了安全起见，不要超过 -0.3 dB，因为这可能会导致老旧播放系统出现问题。下图显示了使用 Cubase 的 Maximizer 插件进行响度优化前后的音频轨道示例。

    Now comes the loudness optimization. Use a limiter (or a maximizer) to push the volume to the desired level. Typical peak volume levels for a pop or rock song after mastering are - 6 dB in the intro or interlude, - 3 dB in the verse and close to 0 dB in the chorus and solo. Play it safe and don't go beyond - 0.3 dB as this might cause problems on older playback systems. In the image below you can see an example audio track before and after loudness optimization using Cubase's Maximizer plugin.













    除了提升音量之外，最终的限幅器还能防止削波及其相关的失真。这当然意味着，此时我们不能再进行任何会影响歌曲动态范围的更改。否则，限幅器的保护作用就会消失。它必须位于处理流程的最后，才能真正起到“防线”的作用。

    Additionally to pushing volume, the final limiter also prevents clipping and the distortions associated with it. This of course means that at this point we cannot make any further changes that will have an impact on the song's dynamics. If we do, we lose the protection of the limiter. It must be last in line to properly serve as a "brick-wall".





    8. 抖动和导出

    8. Dithering And Export





    到目前为止，您应该一直使用 24 位或 32 位音频进行工作。如果您的最终混音作品要刻录到 CD 上，则必须以 16 位格式导出母带处理后的歌曲。为了最大限度地减少转换过程中的量化噪声，请在导出前为混音添加抖动效果。

    Up to now you will (or should) have been working in 24 or 32 bit. If your final mix is meant to go on a CD, you have to export the mastered song in 16 bit. To minimize quantization noise during this conversion, add dither to the mix before exporting.









    -------------------------------------

    -------------------------------------





    背景信息 - 数字化

    Background Info - Digitization





    为了能够在计算机中存储和修改信号，我们必须将连续的模拟信号转换成一系列的0和1。这个过程称为数字化。它分为两个步骤：采样和量化。

    To be able to store and alter a signal in a computer, we have to transform a continuous analog signal into a series of zeros and ones. This process called digitization. It is broken down in two steps: sampling and quantization.





    在采样过程中，模拟信号会以固定的时间间隔进行测量。例如，44.1 kHz 的采样率意味着计算机在一秒钟内读取信号 44100 次。为了在不丢失数据的情况下对信号进行采样（即在采样过程中不改变其频谱的相关部分），采样率至少需要是信号中最高频率的两倍。因此，44.1 kHz 的采样率足以对频率低于 22050 Hz 的信号进行数字化（该频率远高于任何年龄段的听觉阈值）。

    During sampling, the analog signal is measured at regular time intervals. For example, a sampling rate of 44.1 kHz means that the computer reads the signal 44.100 times in one second. To sample a signal without data loss (that is, without changing relevant parts of its spectrum in the process), the sampling rate needs to be at least twice the highest frequency in the signal. Hence, a sampling rate of 44.1 kHz is sufficient to digitize signals that contain frequencies of 22.050 Hz and below (which is well past the threshold of hearing for any age).





    下一步，连续信号值（电压或幅度）会被舍入到一个固定值的网格中。这称为量化。每个固定值都用一行0和1表示。在一个字长为x位的系统中，该网格将包含2^ x个值。例如，一个16位系统可以容纳65,536个固定值。因此，字长越大，网格越精细，模拟信号电压或幅度舍入产生的误差就越小。

    During the next step, the continuous signal values (voltage or amplitude) are rounded to a grid of fixed values. This is called quantization. Each of the fixed values is represented by a line of zeros and ones. In a system with an x bit word size, the grid will contain 2x values. For example, a 16-bit system allows 65.536 fixed values. So the higher the word size, the finer the grid and the smaller the errors that result from rounding the voltage or amplitude of the analog signal.













    （正弦波及其在3位系统中的数字化形式）

    (A sine wave and its digitized form in a 3-bit system)





    在16位（或更高）系统中，量化误差通常是听不到的。但即使在这样的字长下，对于非常微弱的信号，仍然会出现问题。在这种情况下，信号幅度与量化步长处于同一数量级，因此强制将信号映射到网格上会严重扭曲信号，导致“颗粒噪声”。抖动（即向信号添加非常微弱的随机噪声）有助于降低量化噪声。

    The quantization errors are usually not audible in systems with 16-bit (or higher). But even at these word sizes problems can occur for signals that are very soft. In this case the amplitude is in the order of the quantization step and thus forcing the signal onto the grid severely distorts it, resulting in "granular noise". Dithering, the process of adding very weak random noise to the signal, helps to reduce the quantization noise.

    -------------------------------------









    3.3. 中/侧处理

    3.3. Mid/Side Processing

    坚持你的决定，但保持灵活的态度——托尼·罗宾斯

    Stay committed to your decisions, but stay flexible in your approach - Tony Robbins









    中/侧（简称：M/S）母带处理是一种从不同角度处理混音的有趣方法，它能够触及通常在母带处理过程中无法触及的音乐部分。这种方法由来已久，但在过去十年中才真正流行起来。

    Mid/Side (in short: M/S) mastering is an interesting way of approaching the mix from a different perspective and gaining access to parts of the music that are usually not accessible during mastering. It has been around for a long time, but gained significantly in popularity over the past ten years.





    我们通常认为立体声混音由一个左声道 (L) 和一个右声道 (R) 组成。然而，这并非分解立体声信号的唯一方法。我们还可以使用所谓的和(S) 和差(D) 来构建立体声信号。和是将左右声道合并成单声道混音后的结果。它包含左右声道中完全相同的信号，也就是说，所有在两个声道中同时出现且音量相同的信号。

    Commonly we think of a stereo mix as being composed of one left (L) and one right (R) channel. However, this is not the only possible way to break down a stereo signal. We can also construct it using the so-called sum (S) on the one hand and the difference (D) on the other. The sum is what we get when we combine the left and right channel into a mono mix. It contains all the signals that are identical in the left and right channel, that is, all signals that appear at the same time with the same volume in both channels.





    L + R = S

    L + R = S





    剩余部分是左右声道中不同的信号，它们构成了差值。我们通过将左声道与相位反转后的右声道混合成单声道混音来获得这种差值。

    The left-overs are the signals that differ in the left and right channel. They make up the difference. We get the difference by combining the left channel with the phase-inverted right channel into a mono mix.





    L + (-R) = D

    L + (-R) = D





    在 Cubase 中，您可以按照以下步骤操作。首先，导入您想要拆分为和与差的混音文件。导入时请务必选择“拆分声道”，以便您可以分别访问左右声道。

    Here's how you can do it in Cubase. First, import the mix that you'd like to split up in a sum and difference. Make sure to select "split channels" during import so that you have access to the left and right channels separately.













    现在你应该能看到两个声道。合并音频很简单。依次点击“文件”、“导出”和“音频混音”。选择“单声道导出”后导出混音。

    Now you should see both channels in front of you. Creating the sum is easy. Go to "File", "Export" and "Audio Mixdown". Export the mix after selecting "Mono-Export".













    重要提示：混音时左右声道的音量会叠加。因此，为避免削波失真，您需要降低立体声输出的音量。为了安全起见，建议降低 6 dB。

    Important note: the volume of the left and right channel will add during the mixdown. So to avoid clipping you have to lower the volume level of the stereo out. Lower it by - 6 dB to be on the safe side.





    现在我们有了总信号（或中间信号），接下来我们来计算差分信号。退出“音频混音”窗口并打开混音器（F3）。在混音器中，只需单击一个按钮即可反转右声道的相位。在声像滑块上方，您应该会看到一个带有直线穿过的圆圈。激活此按钮即可反转声道相位。

    Now that we have the sum (or mid signal), let's create the difference. Exit the "Audio Mixdown" form and open the mixer (F3). In the mixer you can phase-invert the right channel with the simple click of a button. Just above the pan slider you should see a circle with a straight line going through it. Activate this button to phase-invert the channel.













    完成上述步骤后，返回“音频混音”表单，勾选“单声道导出”并导出。现在我们还有差分信号（或称侧边信号）。将和信号和差分信号都导入到您的项目中。为了便于比较，最好也保留左右声道。如果您不使用左右声道，只需将其静音即可。

    With this done, go back to the "Audio Mixdown" form, check "Mono-Export" and export. Now we also have the difference (or side signal). Import both the sum and difference into your project. It's a good idea to keep the left and right channels as well for comparison. Just mute them if you don't use them.





    我们再进一步细分一下。复制差分音轨。将原始差分音轨完全向左平移，将另一个差分音轨相位反转后完全向右平移。现在你的项目中应该有五个音轨：静音的左右声道、总和音轨、向左平移的差分音轨以及向右平移并相位反转的差分音轨。

    We'll split the difference up a little further. Duplicate the difference track. Pan the original difference track hard to the left, phase-invert the other difference track and pan it hard to the right. Now you should have five tracks in your project: the muted left and right channels, the sum, the difference panned to the left and the difference panned to the right and phase-inverted.





    以下是流程概述：

    Here's a summary of the process:





    1. 导入混音，选择“分离通道”

    1. Import Mix, Select "split channels"

    2. 单一出口→总和

    2. Mono-Export → Sum

    3. 右声道相位反转

    3. Phase-Invert Right Channel

    4. 单一出口→差异

    4. Mono-Export → Difference

    5.导入和与差

    5. Import Sum And Difference

    6. 重复差异轨道

    6. Duplicate Difference Track

    7. 将原始图像平移到左侧，将相位反转的副本图像平移到右侧

    7. Pan Original Left, Pan Phase-Inverted Duplicate Right





    现在，我们不再需要使用左右声道（或简单的左右声道立体声和）进行母带处理，而是可以自由地调整信号的和与差。如何利用这一点来提升歌曲质量呢？M/S 处理的一个重要优势在于，它让我们能够 直接控制立体声像。拓宽或收窄立体声就像增加或减少差分音轨的音量一样简单。

    So now instead of mastering using the left and right channels (or the simple stereo sum of the two), we are free to alter the sum and difference of the signal. How can we use this to improve the song? One important advantage of M/S processing is that it gives us straight-forward control over the stereo image. Widening and narrowing the stereo is as simple as increasing or decreasing the volume level of the difference tracks.





    当然，改变差分信号的音量并非塑造立体声像的唯一方法。原则上，只要能产生悦耳的声音，任何方法都可以。我们可以添加混响或延迟来拉伸差分音轨，使用合唱效果柔化它们，使用激励器添加和声等等……

    Of course changing the volume of difference signals is not the only way to sculpt the stereo image. In principle, everything goes as long as it produces a pleasing sound. We can add reverb or delay to stretch the difference tracks, soften them using chorus, add harmonies using the exciter, etc ...





    M/S 技术也提供了创建真正单声道低音的方法。正如我们在上一章中学到的，将低频成分丰富的乐器放在中间位置是有充分理由的。但即使我们将它们声像定位到中间，差分信号中仍然会残留一些低音。要去除这些低音信号，只需对 差分音轨应用高通滤波器即可。

    The M/S technique also provides the means to create a true mono bass. As we learned in the previous chapter, there are good reasons to keep instruments with lots of low frequency content in the center. But even if we pan them to the center, there will be some bass left in the difference signal. To get rid of these bass signals, simply apply a highpass filter to the difference tracks.





    在对M/S混音应用 压缩器时 ，通常会对和声进行比差声更强的压缩（更低的阈值，更高的压缩比）。这样做有几个积极作用。作为混音基础的和声变得更加稳定，并且随着歌曲响度的增加，立体声像会更加宽广。因此，立体声像会从轻柔部分（例如前奏或间奏）的相对狭窄，转变为响亮部分（例如副歌）的宽广得多。

    When applying compressors to the M/S mix, it is common to compress the sum more strongly (lower threshold, higher ratio) than the difference. This has several positive effects. The sum, which acts as the foundation of the mix, becomes more stable and the stereo image widens as the loudness of the song increases. Hence it goes from relatively narrow in the soft parts (such as intro or interlude) to much wider during loud parts (chorus).









    3.4. 不要放弃

    3.4. Don't Give Up

    在奇迹发生之前，不要放弃——范妮·弗拉格

    Don't give up before the miracle happens - Fannie Flagg









    你认真阅读了这本书，并仔细运用了书中的所有技巧和策略。然而，你却感觉少了点什么。混音听起来并不像你预期的那样“劲爆”和“震撼”。更糟糕的是：听起来一团糟。到底发生了什么？是经验不足造成的。或者更确切地说：是缺乏经验。

    You keenly read this book and carefully applied all the tips and strategies. Yet, you feel there's something missing. The mix simply doesn't sound as "punchy" and "in your face" as you hoped it would. Or even worse: it sounds like a mess. What happened? Experience happened. Or rather: lack thereof.





    达到专业混音和母带处理的水平需要丰富的经验。你必须亲身经历各种陷阱，才能发现它们，并学会如何避免重蹈覆辙。你必须训练自己的耳朵，才能发现问题和不平衡之处。你必须吸收相关知识，才能在不产生新问题的情况下消除这些问题和不平衡。所有这些都需要时间，以及处理大量混音和母带处理糟糕的歌曲。

    Mixing and mastering at a competitive level takes a lot of experience. You have to fall into the traps to notice them and to find out how to avoid them in the future. You have to train your ears to be able to spot problems and imbalances. You have to absorb the knowledge to remove said problems and imbalances without creating new problems. All of this takes time and a ton of horribly mixed and mastered songs.





    别放弃，每个人都是从这里起步的，即使是像Bob Katz这样的混音和母带处理大师也不例外。你的歌曲会随着时间推移而进步，这是毋庸置疑的。要达到竞技水平需要多久？这取决于你有多渴望成功，以及你能投入多少时间。我见过有人在短短几个月内就从“平庸”跃升至“惊艳”。你只需要对这门技艺充满热情，愿意学习基础知识，并进行大量的（不一定每次都成功的）混音和母带处理练习。

    Don't give up, this is where everyone starts, even a mixing and mastering god such as Bob Katz. Your songs will improve with time, it's a sure thing. How long does it take to reach a competitive level? This depends on how much you want it and how much time you are able to invest. I've seen people go from "meh" to "spectacular" within several months. All it takes is a vivid interest in the subject, a willingness to learn the basics and a lot of (not necessarily successful) mixing and mastering sessions.

    4.2 分贝

    4.2. Decibel









    用相对量表示一个量的一种方法是将其与一个参考值进行比较。这有助于我们更好地理解一个量。例如，在力学中，加速度通常与重力加速度相关。与其说加速度是 22 m/s²（除非你懂力学，否则很难理解），我们也可以说加速度是 22 / 9.81 ≈ 2.2 倍重力加速度，或者简单地说 2.2 g（这样更容易理解）。

    A way of expressing a quantity in relative terms is to do the ratio with respect to a reference value. This helps to put a quantity into perspective. For example, in mechanics the acceleration is often expressed in relation to the gravitational acceleration. Instead of saying the acceleration is 22 m/s² (which is hard to relate to unless you know mechanics), we can also say the acceleration is 22 / 9.81 ≈ 2.2 times the gravitational acceleration or simply 2.2 g's (which is much easier to comprehend).





    分贝 (dB) 也是 一种以相对值表示物理量的通用方法，类似于“对数比”。就像对数比一样，它并非物理单位，也不局限于任何特定领域，例如力学、音频等等。你可以用分贝来表示任何物理量。例如，如果我们以重力加速度作为参考值，那么 22 m/s² 的加速度就对应于 3.5 dB。

    The decibel (dB) is also a general way of expressing a quantity in relative terms, sort of a "logarithmic ratio". And just like the ratio, it is not a physical unit or limited to any field such as mechanics, audio, etc ... You can express any quantity in decibels. For example, if we take the reference value to be the gravitational acceleration, the acceleration 22 m/s² corresponds to 3.5 dB.





    要计算量 x 相对于参考值 x₀ 的分贝值 L ，我们可以使用以下公式：

    To calculate the decibel value L of a quantity x relative to the reference value x0, we can use this formula:









    在声学中，分贝用于表示声压级（SPL），声压级的单位是帕斯卡（Pa），听觉阈值（0.00002 Pa）是参考值。然而，在这种情况下，分贝的系数是原来的二十，而不是十。系数的变化是由于输入的是声压值的平方而不是线性值。

    In acoustics the decibel is used to express the sound pressure level (SPL), measured in Pascal = Pa, using the threshold of hearing (0.00002 Pa) as reference. However, in this case a factor of twenty instead of ten is used. The change in factor is a result of inputting the squares of the pressure values rather than the linear values.









    眩晕弹发出的声音峰值声压级约为 15,000 帕斯卡。换算成分贝，这相当于：

    The sound coming from a stun grenade peaks at a sound pressure level of around 15,000 Pa. In decibel terms this is:









    这远远超过了疼痛阈值（约 63.2 帕斯卡/130 分贝）。以下是一些需要记住的典型值：

    which is way past the threshold of pain that is around 63.2 Pa (130 dB). Here are some typical values to keep in mind:





    0 分贝 → 听觉阈值

    0 dB → Threshold of Hearing

    20 分贝 → 耳语

    20 dB → Whispering

    60 分贝 → 正常对话

    60 dB → Normal Conversation

    80 分贝 → 吸尘器

    80 dB → Vacuum Cleaner

    110 分贝 → 摇滚音乐会前排

    110 dB → Front Row at Rock Concert

    130 分贝 → 疼痛阈值

    130 dB → Threshold of Pain

    160 分贝 → 耳膜破裂

    160 dB → Bursting Eardrums





    为什么要用分贝呢？难道用比值来衡量一个量还不够吗？如果量级变化不大，比值当然没问题。我们日常生活中遇到的速度或加速度就属于这种情况。但当量级变化显著，跨越多个数量级时（声压级就是这种情况），分贝就显得更加方便易懂了。

    Why use the decibel at all? Isn't the ratio good enough for putting a quantity into perspective? The ratio works fine as long as the quantity doesn't go over many order of magnitudes. This is the case for the speeds or accelerations that we encounter in our daily lives. But when a quantity varies significantly and spans many orders of magnitude (which is what the SPL does), the decibel is much more handy and relatable.





    使用分贝来衡量音频信号的另一个原因是韦伯-费希纳定律。该定律指出，人们对刺激的感知呈对数而非线性关系。因此，用分贝表示声压级可以被视为对人耳感知声音响度的初步近似，而非从纯粹物理角度来看声音的响度。

    Another reason for using the decibel for audio signals is provided by the Weber-Fechner law. It states that a stimulus is perceived in a logarithmic rather than linear fashion. So expressing the SPL in decibels can be regarded as a first approximation to how loud a sound is perceived by a person as opposed to how loud it is from a purely physical point of view.

    请注意，当两个或多个声源混合时，分贝值并非简单地相加。相反，如果两个声源音量相同且相位一致，则音量会增加 6 分贝（如果相位相反，则增加的音量会小于 6 分贝）。例如，当两个声源的音量均为 50 分贝时，混合后的声音音量将为 56 分贝（或更低）。

    Note that when combining two or more sound sources, the decibel values are not simply added. Rather, if we combine two sources that are equally loud and in phase, the volume increases by 6 dB (if they are out of phase, it will be less than that). For example, when adding two sources that are at 50 dB, the resulting sound will have a volume of 56 dB (or less).
